# The Hang Seng University of Hong Kong (HSUHK) Complete Guide 2026

When Hong Kong students and parents talk about university choices, attention usually centres on the eight UGC-funded "Big 8" institutions. Yet outside that bracket sits a parallel track that is increasingly hard to ignore - the **self-financing universities**. And on that track, **The Hang Seng University of Hong Kong (HSUHK)** is widely regarded as the flagship: it is Hong Kong's largest self-financing private university, founded by The Hang Seng Bank Education Foundation, with an alumni network deeply embedded in the city's banking and financial services sector. In 2024 its School of Business secured **AACSB International accreditation** - the global gold standard for business education held by only **6% of business schools worldwide** and, among Hong Kong self-financing institutions, by **HSUHK alone**.

For HKDSE candidates whose results sit just below Big 8 cut-offs, for non-JUPAS applicants from international or mainland systems, and for those targeting business, communication, translation or supply chain careers, HSUHK is one of the strongest "second-track" options in the city. This guide walks through HSUHK's identity, its 2026 admission requirements (JUPAS, Non-JUPAS, and Gaokao), tuition and scholarships, flagship programmes, and graduate outcomes - so you can decide whether it deserves a place on your application list.

## 1. What kind of university is HSUHK?

### Origins and positioning

HSUHK traces its lineage to **Hang Seng School of Commerce (1980)**, founded by The Hang Seng Bank Education Foundation. It became **Hang Seng Management College in 2010**, and in **2018** received government approval to be retitled **The Hang Seng University of Hong Kong** - the second self-financing private institution in Hong Kong (after Shue Yan University) to attain full university status.

The campus sits on a hillside in **Siu Lek Yuen, Sha Tin**, a short walk from MTR Shek Mun station, with a true "one-stop campus" layout that few self-financing peers can match. HSUHK's positioning is "**liberal arts plus profession**": small-class teaching (staff-to-student ratio around 1:18), compulsory residential education for all undergraduates, and an applied, employer-aligned curriculum.

### Scale and faculty

- **Undergraduates**: roughly 6,000 - the largest private undergraduate body in Hong Kong outside the Big 8
- **Faculty**: around 350 full-time academics, **over 80% holding doctoral degrees**
- **Schools**: 6 (Business; Communication; Decision Sciences; Humanities and Social Science; Translation and Foreign Languages; and Transdisciplinary Studies)
- **Undergraduate programmes**: **27 four-year honours degrees**
- **Non-local students**: roughly 12% of the cohort

### Rankings and accreditation

- **AppliedHE ALL ASIA Private University Ranking 2026**: Greater China #7
- **QS Asia University Rankings 2026**: Greater China #157 band
- **THE Young University Rankings**: 351-400 globally
- **AACSB International** accreditation for the School of Business (2024) - one of only six AACSB-accredited business schools in Hong Kong
- **Professional accreditation** for individual programmes from ACCA, HKICPA, CIMA, ANZIIF, CILT and others

HSUHK does not feature in the QS World University Rankings main table, but among Hong Kong employers - especially in banking, accountancy, insurance and supply chain - its graduates carry significant brand recognition. HSBC, Hang Seng Bank, the Big Four accounting firms, and licensed local securities houses consistently hire HSUHK graduates each year.

## 2. The six schools and 27 undergraduate programmes

### School of Business (AACSB-accredited)

The flagship school, accounting for nearly half the undergraduate cohort. Programmes include:

- BBA (Hons) in Banking and Finance
- BBA (Hons) in Professional Accountancy (HKICPA / ACCA-accredited)
- BBA (Hons) in Management
- BBA (Hons) in Marketing
- BBA (Hons) in Human Resource Management
- BBA (Hons) in Economics
- BBA (Hons) in Supply Chain Management (CILT-accredited)
- BBA (Hons) in Convention and Event Management
- BBA (Hons) in Insurance and Risk Management (ANZIIF-accredited)
- BBA (Hons) in Financial Analysis

### School of Communication

A regional reputation in journalism and convergent media:

- BA (Hons) in Journalism and Communication
- BA (Hons) in Convergent Media and Communication Technology

The school is known for its dual-language newsroom training and a strong record placing graduates with TVB, Now TV, RTHK, Bloomberg and South China Morning Post.

### School of Decision Sciences

- BSc (Hons) in Computing and Decision Sciences
- BSc (Hons) in Data Science and Business Intelligence
- BSc (Hons) in Financial Analytics
- BSc (Hons) in Supply Chain Management and Analytics

### School of Humanities and Social Science

- BA (Hons) in English
- BSocSc (Hons) in Applied Sociology
- BSocSc (Hons) in Applied and Human-Centred Computing
- BA (Hons) in Cultural and Creative Industries

### School of Translation and Foreign Languages

A signature HSUHK strength, backed by a graduate Translation School:

- BTM (Hons) in Translation with Business
- BA (Hons) in Translation with Business (Chinese-English)
- BA (Hons) in Bilingual Communication for Business

### School of Transdisciplinary Studies

A newer school created to host interdisciplinary degrees combining humanities, technology and business.

## 3. JUPAS admission (HKDSE candidates)

HSUHK has participated in the **JUPAS Admissions Scheme** since the 2024-25 cycle for selected programmes, and accepts **direct application** through its own admission portal in parallel.

### Minimum HKDSE entry requirement

- **Chinese Language**: Level 3
- **English Language**: Level 3
- **Mathematics (Compulsory Part)**: Level 2
- **Citizenship and Social Development**: Attained
- **One elective subject**: Level 2

The **3-3-2-2-2** profile is the floor; competitive programmes (BBA Banking and Finance, BBA Professional Accountancy, BA Journalism, BA Translation with Business) typically admit students at **Level 4 in Chinese and English** with **3-4 in core subjects**.

### How HSUHK calculates JUPAS scores

HSUHK uses the **best 5 subjects** model - including Chinese, English, Mathematics (Compulsory Part), and the two best elective or M1/M2 results - converted to a 35-point scale. Unlike some Big 8 programmes that double-weight specific subjects, HSUHK applies a relatively flat weighting, which can favour balanced candidates.

### Key dates (JUPAS cycle 2026)

- **Programme choices submitted**: by early December 2025
- **Programme choice modification**: post-results, July 2026
- **Main round offers**: early August 2026 (after HKDSE release)

### Direct (Non-JUPAS) parallel application

HSUHK also accepts direct DSE applications outside JUPAS for the same programmes, enabling candidates to receive an **early conditional offer** based on predicted grades - a useful insurance policy if your JUPAS Band A choices are competitive.

## 4. Non-JUPAS admission (international and mainland qualifications)

HSUHK welcomes applicants holding:

- **GCE A-Level / IAL**: typically 3 A-Levels at **CCC or above** for general entry, **BBC** for competitive programmes
- **IB Diploma**: minimum **24 points** overall, **30+** for competitive programmes
- **SAT / ACT**: combined SAT 1100+ (EBRW + Math), with strong English subscores
- **Associate Degree / Higher Diploma**: senior-year entry available - HSUHK is one of the most active receivers of Hong Kong sub-degree articulation
- **Other recognised national qualifications** (Australian ATAR, Canadian provincial diplomas, etc.)

### English language requirement

For applicants whose senior secondary medium of instruction was not English:

- **IELTS**: 6.0 overall (no band below 5.5)
- **TOEFL iBT**: 70+
- **HKDSE English**: Level 3+
- **GCE / IGCSE English**: Grade C / Level 4+

### Application timeline (Non-JUPAS / International, 2026 entry)

- **Round 1 deadline**: 30 April 2026
- **Round 2 deadline**: 30 June 2026
- **Rolling decisions** typically issued within 4-6 weeks of complete submission

## 5. Mainland Gaokao admission (Independent Recruitment)

Beginning in the **2025-26 academic year**, HSUHK was approved by China's Ministry of Education to expand its **Independent Recruitment Scheme to all 31 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities** (previously around 20). The 2026 intake quota has been increased from 450 to **750 students**, with **no per-province cap** - meaning candidates are not blocked because their province's quota is full.

### Gaokao score thresholds

| Item | Minimum requirement |
|---|---|
| Total Gaokao score | At or above the **first-tier line (一本线 / 本科线)** in the candidate's province; certain programmes accept second-tier line |
| English subject score | **100/150** (this is a hard cut-off, applied uniformly across all programmes) |
| Interview | Online English interview required for shortlisted candidates |

### Application window

- **Online application opens**: October 2025
- **Application deadline**: late June 2026 (typically 22 June)
- **Interviews**: rolling, June-July 2026
- **Offer release**: early-mid July 2026, ahead of the mainland regular admission round

A critical feature: HSUHK admission **does not occupy a slot in the mainland centralised college admission system (统招)**. Students who receive an HSUHK offer remain free to participate in mainland Gaokao admission and can choose between the two offers.

## 6. Tuition fees and total cost (2026-27)

### Tuition

- **Local (HKDSE / JUPAS) students**: HK$95,000 per year (most BBA / BA programmes); the Hong Kong SAR Government **Non-means-tested Subsidy Scheme for Self-financing Undergraduate Studies (NMTSS)** provides up to **HK$36,260** per year, bringing net tuition for eligible local students to roughly **HK$58,740**
- **Non-local students (mainland and international)**: approximately **HK$100,000-110,000 per year** (around USD 12,800)

### Living costs

For non-local students residing in Hong Kong, total annual cost (tuition plus accommodation, meals, transport, books, insurance) typically ranges **HK$160,000 - HK$200,000**. HSUHK guarantees first-year on-campus residence for non-local undergraduates; subsequent years can be on-campus (subject to ballot) or in nearby Sha Tin / Tai Wai private rentals (HK$5,000-9,000 per month for a shared flat).

## 7. Scholarships

HSUHK runs one of the more generous self-financing scholarship programmes:

- **Talent Admission Scheme**: **full tuition waiver** (renewable annually subject to GPA) for HKDSE students with five subjects at Level 5 or above, or Gaokao students 50+ points above the first-tier line
- **Entrance Scholarships**: HK$30,000 - HK$60,000 one-off awards for outstanding new entrants
- **President's Scholarships**: full tuition plus living stipend, for the highest-scoring entrants per school
- **Need-based bursaries**: for non-local students with documented financial need
- **Programme-specific awards** in Translation, Journalism, Supply Chain and Data Science

## 8. Flagship programmes - what HSUHK does best

### BBA in Professional Accountancy

The most established programme, holding **HKICPA, ACCA and CPA Australia** accreditation. Graduates routinely place into the Big Four (Deloitte, EY, KPMG, PwC) graduate intakes - in some recent years HSUHK was the second-largest source of Big Four campus hires in Hong Kong after CUHK Business School.

### BBA in Banking and Finance

Leverages the Hang Seng Bank heritage. Curriculum covers retail banking, wealth management, FinTech, and CFA Level I content. Internship pipelines into Hang Seng Bank, HSBC, Bank of China (Hong Kong) and Standard Chartered.

### BBA in Supply Chain Management

CILT-accredited; the **MSc in Global Supply Chain Management** at HSUHK ranked **84th globally in QS International Trade Rankings 2025**, indicating real research weight in this niche. The undergraduate programme runs two pathways - "academic / further study" and "professional practice" - allowing students to build either toward an MSc or directly into logistics employment with companies like DHL, Kerry Logistics and Cathay Cargo.

### BA in Journalism and Communication

Strong placement track at TVB, Now TV, RTHK, SCMP and Bloomberg. The school operates dual-language student newsrooms and a TV studio facility comparable in equipment to Big 8 journalism schools.

### BA in Translation with Business

HSUHK's translation programmes are ranked alongside CUHK and PolyU as the top three in Hong Kong by industry surveys. The "with Business" specialisation - combining commercial translation, business communication and bilingual editing - is genuinely distinctive and feeds directly into demand from law firms, banks, and the Hong Kong civil service.

## 9. Career outcomes

HSUHK publishes annual graduate employment surveys; recent cohorts show:

- **Overall employment rate (within 6 months)**: 95%+
- **Average starting monthly salary (2024 graduates)**: roughly **HK$22,000 - HK$25,000**, with BBA Banking and Finance and BBA Professional Accountancy graduates averaging **HK$26,000 - HK$28,000**
- **Top employers**: HSBC, Hang Seng Bank, Bank of China (HK), Big Four accounting firms, AIA, Prudential, Cathay Pacific, DHL, MTR Corporation, Hong Kong civil service
- **Postgraduate progression**: roughly 18-20% of graduates pursue a master's degree within two years, mostly at HKU, CUHK, HKUST, PolyU or overseas universities

For non-local graduates, the **IANG (Immigration Arrangements for Non-local Graduates)** visa applies in full - HSUHK degrees are recognised under the Qualifications Framework, and graduates can stay in Hong Kong for **24 months** (extendable) to work without first securing a job offer.

## 10. Should HSUHK be on your list?

HSUHK is the right choice if you:

- Are an HKDSE candidate scoring in the **18-24 (best 5)** range, and want a recognised, residential, English-medium degree pathway
- Target **business, accountancy, banking, communication, translation or supply chain** careers in Hong Kong
- Are a mainland Gaokao student at or just above the **first-tier line** with strong English (100+/150), and want a Hong Kong degree without the Big 8 cut-throat competition
- Hold international qualifications (A-Level / IB / SAT) and want a Hong Kong option that responds quickly with rolling decisions
- Value **AACSB-accredited business education** but are priced out of, or competitively shut out of, CUHK, HKU and HKUST business schools

It is less suitable if your target is research-intensive STEM, medicine / dentistry, law, or top-tier global rankings prestige - those remain Big 8 territory.

In a crowded Hong Kong undergraduate landscape, HSUHK has carved out a clear position: the **strongest self-financing brand**, the **only AACSB business school outside the Big 8**, and a **professional, employment-focused** degree experience on a genuine campus. For the right student, it is not a fallback - it is a deliberate choice.

# HKU vs CUHK vs HKUST: A Comprehensive Comparison for DSE Students

Choosing between the University of Hong Kong (HKU), The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), and The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) is one of the most consequential decisions a DSE candidate will make. All three are ranked among the world's top universities, yet they differ meaningfully in history, campus culture, academic strengths, and the type of student who thrives within each environment.

This guide cuts through the noise. It presents an honest, side-by-side analysis so you can match your academic goals, personality, and career ambitions to the institution most likely to help you succeed.

---

## 1. History and Identity

### HKU — The Colonial Flagship

Founded in 1911, the University of Hong Kong is the oldest and most internationally recognized of the three. Its Pok Fu Lam campus sits on the western edge of Hong Kong Island, overlooking the harbour. HKU was built in the British colonial model — liberal arts breadth, emphasis on professional schools (Medicine, Law, Business), and a cosmopolitan, English-first environment.

HKU's identity is shaped by prestige and tradition. The university produces a disproportionate share of Hong Kong's judges, surgeons, bankers, and civil servants. For over a century it has been the default aspiration of the city's top-scoring secondary students. That institutional gravity is real: the HKU brand opens doors in Hong Kong, the UK, and across Commonwealth networks in a way that is difficult to replicate.

### CUHK — The Bilingual Research University

Established in 1963, CUHK was created as a federation of three existing colleges — New Asia, Chung Chi, and United — each with its own campus residence culture. This collegiate structure remains CUHK's most distinctive feature: students belong to a college, not just a faculty, and college life (sports, drama, service, orientation camps) is genuinely central to the undergraduate experience.

CUHK is the only university in Hong Kong where Chinese and English share equal institutional status. Its campus in Sha Tin occupies the largest footprint of any university in the territory, with a proper town-within-a-campus feel, its own MTR station, and a cultural life that arguably matches many residential universities elsewhere. For students who want a rich four-year campus experience rather than a commuter degree, CUHK's campus is in a class of its own.

### HKUST — The Science and Technology Powerhouse

Founded as recently as 1991, HKUST is the youngest of the three and by far the fastest climber in global rankings. Built on a cliff above Clear Water Bay, the campus is compact, functional, and purpose-built for science, technology, engineering, and business. HKUST's founding mandate was explicit: to become a world-class research university focused on STEM and business, and to help transform Hong Kong's economy.

HKUST achieved that mandate with remarkable speed. Within three decades of opening it had placed inside the global top 40 in the QS World University Rankings — a trajectory almost without precedent. Its culture is high-pressure, meritocratic, and distinctly international, with a student body drawn from mainland China, Southeast Asia, the West, and Hong Kong in roughly equal proportion.

---

Key takeaway: HKU leads in overall global brand recognition and medicine. HKUST punches above its size in STEM and business. CUHK is competitive across the board and, in certain subjects (finance, Chinese studies, social sciences), has programmes that rival or exceed the other two.

## 4. Programme Strengths — Where Each University Leads

### HKU's Strongest Programmes

**Medicine and Health Sciences.** HKU Medicine is routinely ranked among the top 30 medical schools in the world. The Queen Mary Hospital teaching network and research output — notably in virology and epidemiology — give HKU a genuine global edge. For DSE students with 44+ aggregate who are committed to a clinical career, HKU Medicine remains the gold standard in Asia.

**Law.** HKU's Faculty of Law has the deepest alumni network in Hong Kong's legal profession and the strongest connections to commercial law firms in London, Singapore, and New York. Common Law training at HKU carries particular weight in international arbitration.

**Architecture and Built Environment.** HKU's Faculty of Architecture is the most established in Hong Kong and produces a high proportion of the city's practising architects, planners, and surveyors.

**Social Sciences and Humanities.** HKU's liberal arts tradition means its social sciences faculty — particularly sociology, political science, and economics — has attracted internationally recognized scholars. The interdisciplinary Global Challenges programme and various capstone research tracks are genuinely rigorous.

### CUHK's Strongest Programmes

**Finance and Accounting.** CUHK Business School (CUBS) and its constituent School of Accountancy are regarded by the Big Four accounting firms as Hong Kong's premier training ground. CUHK consistently produces more CPA-qualified graduates in Hong Kong than any other institution.

**Chinese Studies and Translation.** No university in Hong Kong — or arguably the broader Chinese-speaking world — rivals CUHK's depth in classical and modern Chinese studies, Chinese literature, translation, and Sinology. The department's research output and faculty pedigree are exceptional.

**Medical Sciences and Pharmacy.** CUHK's Faculty of Medicine at Prince of Wales Hospital has world-class research in gastroenterology, minimally invasive surgery, and Chinese medicine integration. The Faculty of Pharmacy, opened in 2012, has grown rapidly.

**Social Sciences and Communication.** CUHK's journalism, communication, and social policy programmes have strong practitioner networks in Hong Kong's media, NGO, and public sector. The School of Journalism and Communication has produced a significant share of the territory's working journalists.

**Education.** CUHK's Faculty of Education is the largest and most research-active education faculty among the three universities, with close ties to school networks across Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area.

### HKUST's Strongest Programmes

**Computer Science and AI.** HKUST's Department of Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) ranks among the top 30 globally in multiple systems. Faculty research in AI, machine learning, robotics, and distributed systems is world-class. Tech recruiting from HKUST's CSE by Google, Meta, ByteDance, Huawei, and regional startups is consistently strong.

**Engineering (broadly).** Whether electronic engineering, chemical engineering, civil engineering, or industrial engineering — HKUST's engineering faculty have the highest research output per capita of any Hong Kong institution. The university's industry ties to semiconductor and technology firms are deep.

**Business (Kellogg-HKUST EMBA).** The joint Kellogg-HKUST EMBA programme has ranked #1 globally multiple times. While this is a postgraduate programme, it reflects the School of Business and Management's international standing and global network, which flows down to undergraduate business students through alumni connections and faculty quality.

**Data Science and Statistics.** HKUST was early to build out data science as a standalone discipline. Its BSc in Data Science & Technology and MSc programmes feed directly into quant finance, tech, and consulting roles.

**Environmental and Sustainability Sciences.** HKUST's oceanography, atmospheric science, and sustainability research programmes are internationally recognized, with strong connections to regional government policy work.

---

## 5. Campus Life and Culture

### HKU: Urban, Cosmopolitan, Ambitious

HKU's campus in Pok Fu Lam is beautiful but compact. Most students commute or live in university halls with limited capacity relative to enrolment. The campus has a professional, slightly formal atmosphere — students dress for lectures, societies are numerous and well-organized, and there is a strong culture of internship-chasing from Year 1.

The student body is genuinely international: roughly 30–35% of undergraduates are non-local. English is the unquestioned language of instruction and social interaction for most students. For students who want to build international friendships and practice English immersion, HKU's environment delivers that naturally.

The downside: the campus can feel transactional. With many students commuting and a culture oriented toward professional outcomes, the spontaneous social bonding of a residential campus is harder to find. Common Room culture and hall sports are active, but not universal.

**Best fit**: Students who are self-directed, career-focused, comfortable in English-dominant environments, and want the most internationally recognized Hong Kong degree.

### CUHK: Residential, Bilingual, Community-Oriented

CUHK's sprawling Sha Tin campus is genuinely one of Asia's most liveable university environments. The majority of Year 1 students live on campus (university guarantee), and the College system means every student has a smaller community — a dining hall, common rooms, sports teams, and a mentorship culture — embedded within the larger university.

Chinese and English coexist naturally. Lectures are typically in English; corridor conversations and college activities flow between Cantonese, Mandarin, and English depending on context. Students from the mainland and Southeast Asia integrate relatively naturally because neither English nor Chinese is exclusively dominant.

The campus has its own shopping mall, medical facilities, post office, and MTR station (University Station). Students genuinely spend most of their undergraduate years within the campus ecosystem. This produces strong year-group bonds and lifelong alumni networks.

The downside: the campus's self-contained nature can create a slight insularity. Some graduates report having to adjust more deliberately to off-campus professional environments after leaving.

**Best fit**: Students who want a rich four-year community experience, are drawn to bilingual environments, value Chinese cultural depth, or are entering fields where CUHK's networks (finance, accounting, education, Chinese studies) are strongest.

### HKUST: High-Intensity, Global, Results-Driven

HKUST's Clear Water Bay campus is visually striking — perched above the sea with a dramatic atrium that functions as the university's social heart. Residential capacity is relatively high, and a significant proportion of Year 1 students live on campus. The culture is competitive, collaborative, and intensely focused on outcomes: research publications, hackathon wins, internship offers, and graduate school admissions.

The student body is among the most internationally diverse in Hong Kong, with a large mainland Chinese cohort, significant Southeast Asian representation, and exchange students from Europe and North America. English is the primary language of instruction and most formal interaction; Mandarin is widely spoken socially.

The campus's relative remoteness (Clear Water Bay requires a bus or shuttle to reach MTR) creates a self-contained intensity. Students often joke that HKUST's isolation either bonds you deeply with classmates or burns you out — there is some truth to both.

**Best fit**: Students who are STEM-inclined, self-driven, comfortable in a competitive international environment, and targeting technology, quant finance, research, or global consulting careers.

---

## 6. Research Output and Innovation Ecosystem

Research performance matters for the quality of teaching faculty you'll learn from and for research assistant/internship opportunities during your undergraduate years.

| Metric | HKU | CUHK | HKUST |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nature Index (2024) | High | High | Very High |
| Research grants (competitive, HKD bn, approx.) | 3.0+ | 2.5+ | 2.8+ |
| Spin-off companies founded | 100+ | 80+ | 180+ |
| US patents granted (cumulative) | Significant | Significant | Among highest in HK |
| Industry research collaborations | Strong (medical, legal) | Strong (finance, social) | Very Strong (tech, engineering) |

HKUST's technology transfer and startup ecosystem is the most active: it has produced unicorn companies (SenseTime, DJI received early links to HKUST faculty), and its Entrepreneurship Center is a recognized regional hub. For students interested in deep tech or starting companies, HKUST's ecosystem is materially stronger.

HKU leads in clinical research and health sciences. CUHK leads in Chinese medicine integration, social science policy research, and education research.

---

## 7. Career Placement and Graduate Outcomes

### Finance and Banking

All three universities are well-represented in Hong Kong's investment banks, asset managers, and Big Four accounting firms. However:

- **CUHK** has the deepest penetration in accounting and retail banking; the CUBUS Finance Society alumni network at Big Four firms is well documented.
- **HKU** leads in international finance — Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Magic Circle law firms recruit HKU heavily for Hong Kong and regional roles.
- **HKUST** leads in quant finance, fintech, and data-driven investment roles; its mathematics and data science graduates are recruited by hedge funds and proprietary trading firms.

### Technology

**HKUST** is clearly the strongest pipeline into regional and global tech companies. ByteDance, Tencent, Alibaba, Meituan, Google, and regional unicorns all recruit actively on campus. CUHK and HKU also have tech recruiting, but HKUST's department-level industry relationships and research reputation make it the first call for many technical roles.

### Medicine and Healthcare

**HKU** and **CUHK** both run MBBS programmes. Both produce competent clinicians and researchers. HKU's slightly higher global ranking and larger teaching hospital network give it a marginal edge for international clinical fellowships. Within Hong Kong, both are equally respected.

### Government and Public Sector

**HKU** historically dominates Hong Kong's Administrative Officer (AO) grade and senior civil service. The AO intake disproportionately recruits from HKU, though CUHK has been closing the gap.

### Graduate School Admissions (Overseas)

All three universities send graduates to top-10 PhD programmes globally. HKUST's research culture makes it particularly strong for STEM PhD placements to MIT, Caltech, Stanford, and ETH Zurich. HKU's law and social science graduates are well-placed for UK and US graduate school. CUHK's bilingual graduates often pursue graduate study in both English-language and Chinese-language academic settings.

---

## 8. JUPAS Band A Strategy Considerations

The JUPAS system allows you to rank up to 25 choices, with Band A being your highest five preferences. Strategic allocation of Band A choices across HKU, CUHK, and HKUST requires understanding both your aggregate score and which specific programmes are most critical to your goals.

### Core strategic principles

**Do not waste Band A slots on programmes you would not attend.** Band A choices should reflect genuine preferences. Admissions offices can detect serial high-low applications, and some programmes interview or consider preference order.

**Consider programme fit over institutional prestige.** If you are committed to Computer Science, HKUST's CS department is a stronger specific choice than HKU's CS offering for many career trajectories, even if HKU's overall brand is higher-ranked. Subject-level rankings matter more than institutional rankings for your actual education.

**Use CUHK as a strategic middle band for borderline aggregates.** CUHK's admission thresholds for many non-medicine programmes are slightly lower than HKU equivalents but offer comparable career outcomes, particularly in business, social sciences, and Chinese studies. A well-matched CUHK programme in Band A can be both aspirational and achievable.

**For STEM candidates with 36–40 aggregate**: HKUST engineering and computer science programmes are typically more attainable than HKU equivalents at similar aggregate scores, and HKUST's technical education and career placement in STEM are superior. Placing HKUST STEM programmes in Band A is often the optimal strategy.

**For medicine aspirants**: HKU and CUHK Medicine both require 43+ aggregates. Place whichever you prefer first, and consider having the other as a strong Band A backup. Both are genuinely world-class — do not agonize excessively over the choice between them.

**For humanities and social sciences students**: CUHK's offerings in Chinese studies, translation, social sciences, and journalism are best-in-class in Hong Kong and often undersubscribed relative to their quality. Placing a CUHK humanities programme in Band A if your aggregate is 33–37 is frequently the highest-return choice.

### Specific Band A configurations worth considering

| Profile | Suggested Band A Configuration |
|---|---|
| 43+ aggregate, medicine-bound | HKU Medicine (1st), CUHK Medicine (2nd), HKU Dentistry (3rd) |
| 40–42 aggregate, law/finance | HKU Law, CUHK Law, HKU BBA, CUHK BBA Finance |
| 37–40 aggregate, STEM-focused | HKUST CS, HKUST BEng, HKU CS, CUHK IE |
| 36–39 aggregate, business-focused | HKUST BBA Global Business, CUHK BBA Finance, HKU BBA |
| 33–37 aggregate, humanities/social sciences | CUHK Social Sciences, CUHK Chinese Studies, HKU Social Sciences |

---

## 9. The Fit Question — Which Student Belongs Where?

Rankings and scores aside, the question of fit matters more than most applicants acknowledge. Students who choose the wrong institutional culture for their personality often struggle, even if their score was sufficient for admission.

### You are likely to thrive at HKU if:

- You are comfortable conducting nearly all academic and social life in English
- You are career-focused and self-directed from Year 1
- Your target profession has a strong HKU alumni pipeline (law, medicine, civil service, international banking)
- You are comfortable in an urban commuter culture and will actively build your own social networks
- International recognition of your degree matters to you for overseas career or graduate school plans

### You are likely to thrive at CUHK if:

- You want a full campus residential experience and a strong college community
- You are bilingual and value operating naturally in both Chinese and English
- Your intended field is finance/accounting, Chinese studies, education, social policy, or journalism
- You are interested in Chinese culture, Chinese philosophy, or research with a Chinese dimension
- You want the warmth of a collegiate culture where identities are formed as much through hall sports and service as through academic performance

### You are likely to thrive at HKUST if:

- You are genuinely passionate about STEM, data, or quantitative finance
- You thrive in competitive, merit-driven environments
- You are internationally oriented and comfortable in a majority non-local student cohort
- Your career targets are in technology, deep tech research, quant roles, or global STEM-adjacent consulting
- You are motivated by proximity to cutting-edge research and industry from Year 1

---

## Key Takeaways

**HKU** is Hong Kong's most internationally recognized university brand, and its medicine, law, and social science programmes carry weight that is difficult to replicate elsewhere. Choose HKU if prestige, international recognition, and professional school access are your primary criteria — and if you are prepared to be self-driven in an English-dominant urban environment.

**CUHK** offers the best all-round undergraduate experience in Hong Kong: a genuine residential campus, a bilingual culture, collegiate identity, and programmes in finance, accounting, Chinese studies, and social sciences that are best-in-class. The CUHK brand is fully respected in Hong Kong and increasingly in the broader Sinophone world. Do not underestimate it relative to HKU simply because its global ranking is lower.

**HKUST** is the correct choice for students who are STEM-serious, internationally ambitious, and targeting technology or quantitative careers. In STEM subjects, its teaching quality and career placement rival institutions ranked significantly higher globally. Its rapid ascent in rankings reflects genuine research excellence that matters in the classroom and in the lab.

For most DSE students, the honest answer is: **the right university is the one where your target programme is strongest, not the one with the highest composite ranking.** A HKUST Computer Science graduate will generally outperform an HKU Computer Science graduate in technical hiring. A CUHK Finance and Investment Analysis graduate enters accounting with stronger immediate networks than equivalents elsewhere. Match your choice to your discipline, not just to a number.

Finally, remember that your university is a starting line, not a finishing line. All three universities have produced exceptional graduates across every field. The habits, relationships, and intellectual curiosity you build in four years matter more than the institution's rank. Choose the environment in which you are most likely to thrive, work hard, and use the full resources available to you.

# The Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts (HKAPA) Complete Guide 2026

When Hong Kong students and parents discuss "the universities," conversation usually orbits the eight UGC-funded institutions - HKU, CUHK, HKUST, PolyU, CityU, HKBU, EdUHK and Lingnan. Sitting alongside the Big 8, however, is a publicly funded institution that does not appear in the JUPAS league table at all and yet ranks ahead of every Hong Kong university in its own discipline: **The Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts (HKAPA / "the Academy" / 演藝學院)**. In the **2026 QS World University Rankings by Subject**, HKAPA placed **10th globally and 1st in Asia for Performing Arts** - a 10-place leap from its 2025 position and one of only five Hong Kong subject entries to break into the world top 10.

For HKDSE candidates whose talent and ambition lie in Chinese opera, dance, drama, film and television, music, or theatre and entertainment arts, HKAPA is in a league of its own. The application logic is also unlike any other Hong Kong university: HKAPA is **not part of JUPAS**, it does not consider Best 5 / Best 6 scores in the conventional way, and the deciding factor is almost always the **audition, portfolio or interview**, not the academic transcript. This guide walks DSE candidates and overseas applicants through HKAPA's identity, the six Schools, 2026/27 admission requirements, tuition and scholarships, flagship programmes and graduate outcomes - so you can decide whether the Academy belongs on your application list.

## 1. What kind of institution is HKAPA?

### Origins and positioning

HKAPA was established by Hong Kong government ordinance in **1984** to provide professional, practice-based training in the performing arts. It is a **statutory tertiary institution funded by the University Grants Committee (UGC)** through a separate funding arrangement, distinct from the eight UGC-funded universities. Its mandate is narrow but globally significant: to be the leading performing arts conservatoire in Asia and a feeder of professional artists, performers, designers and technicians to Hong Kong, the Greater Bay Area and international stages.

The main campus on **Gloucester Road, Wan Chai** - directly opposite the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre - is itself a working performing arts complex, housing the 1,181-seat Lyric Theatre, the Drama Theatre, the Concert Hall, the Studio Theatre, multiple recital halls, dance studios, sound stages, post-production suites and design workshops. A second campus, the **Béthanie** in Pok Fu Lam (a restored 19th-century Gothic Revival sanatorium), houses the School of Film and Television.

### Scale and faculty

- **Total student body**: approximately 1,000 across all programme levels (Diploma, Advanced Diploma, Bachelor's, Master's, MFA)
- **Schools**: six discipline-based Schools (see Section 2)
- **Faculty**: a mix of full-time academics and adjunct industry professionals - working choreographers, conductors, opera principals, film directors, lighting designers, stage managers - which is unusual even by international conservatoire standards
- **Languages of instruction**: English for most academic teaching; Cantonese, Putonghua and English in studio / rehearsal contexts depending on School
- **Performances per year**: HKAPA students stage over **150 public performances** annually, giving every undergraduate substantial public-stage experience before graduation

### Why HKAPA is "the ninth institution" people forget

Because HKAPA is outside JUPAS and does not award the kind of conventional academic degrees families compare on rankings tables, it is often overlooked by mainstream DSE candidates. Yet it is government-funded, awards UGC-recognised degrees (Bachelor of Fine Arts (Honours), Bachelor of Music (Honours)), and graduates qualify for the same post-study work and PR pathways (IANG visa, seven-year permanent residence) as Big 8 graduates. For the right candidate, it is the single most prestigious place to study performing arts anywhere east of London.

## 2. The six Schools

HKAPA's undergraduate offering is organised into six Schools, each with its own faculty, studios and audition panel.

### School of Chinese Opera

The only degree-awarding institution in the world dedicated to **Cantonese opera (粵劇)** at conservatoire level. Streams include performing (singing, acting, fighting), Cantonese opera music, and percussion. Cantonese opera is recognised by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage, and HKAPA is the principal pipeline for new generation principals at major Hong Kong opera houses.

### School of Dance

Three streams: **Ballet, Chinese Dance, and Contemporary Dance**. The School works with the Hong Kong Ballet, City Contemporary Dance Company and Hong Kong Dance Company on residencies and choreographic placements. Auditions test technique, improvisation and a solo in the chosen major.

### School of Drama

Streams in **Acting, Directing and Playwriting**. Teaching combines Stanislavski-rooted Western actor training with Cantonese-language dramatic practice. Productions run year-round at the Drama Theatre and Studio Theatre.

### School of Film and Television

Streams in **Directing, Cinematography, Producing, Screenwriting, Editing, Sound, and Production Design for Film**. Based at the Béthanie campus, with full sound stages, location vehicles, ARRI / RED camera packages and post-production suites. Graduates feed directly into Hong Kong's film and streaming industry and have placed strongly at the Hong Kong Film Awards and the Fresh Wave Festival.

### School of Music

Hong Kong's leading conservatoire-style music school. Streams across **strings, winds, brass, percussion, piano, voice, Chinese music (Erhu, Pipa, Zheng, Dizi, Sheng, etc.), composition and conducting**. Faculty includes principals from the Hong Kong Philharmonic, the Hong Kong Chinese Orchestra and the Hong Kong Sinfonietta. The Concert Hall hosts weekly student recitals.

### School of Theatre and Entertainment Arts

The "behind the curtain" School. Streams in **Stage and Event Management, Technical Direction, Set and Costume Design, Lighting Design, Sound Design, Theatre Design and Property Making, and Arts and Event Management**. The Bachelor of Fine Arts (Honours) in Theatre and Entertainment Arts is one of HKAPA's most internationally recruited programmes, and graduates work across theatre, film, theme parks, K-pop touring production, e-sports stagecraft and major event delivery (M+, West Kowloon, the Hong Kong Sevens, Disney parks).

## 3. 2026/27 admission pathways

HKAPA's admission system is fundamentally **audition-based**. Academic results matter, but only as a baseline; the panel decides on artistic potential.

### General Academic Requirement (HKDSE)

For the four-year Bachelor's programmes, HKDSE candidates need to meet HKAPA's General Academic Requirement, which is broadly:

- **Level 3** in English Language
- **Level 3** in Chinese Language
- **Level 2** in Mathematics (Compulsory Part)
- An **"Attained"** result in Citizenship and Social Development (CSD)
- **Level 2** in at least one elective subject

This is roughly equivalent to "**3322 + 2 elective**" expressed in HKAPA's own language - lower than the Big 8 minimum (typically 332233) but never the deciding factor. Even a perfect academic profile will not secure an offer without a successful audition.

### Non-JUPAS, mainland Gaokao and international applicants

HKAPA does not participate in JUPAS. **All applicants** - HKDSE, mainland Gaokao, IB, GCE A-Level, BTEC, overseas - apply through the **same single application portal** at hkapa.edu. There is no Band A / Band B logic and no mainland JEE-style score cut-off.

- **Mainland Gaokao** candidates need to meet the General Academic Requirement-equivalent (typically a benchmark above the Provincial First Tier line is treated as a positive academic indicator, but it is not a hard cut-off)
- **IB** applicants typically need IB scores meeting or exceeding the equivalent of HKAPA GAR (often 24+ with English at Standard Level 4 or Higher Level 3+)
- **A-Level** applicants typically need 2 A-Level passes plus GCSE-level English

### English language requirement

For applicants whose previous education was not in English, HKAPA accepts **IELTS Academic 5.5 overall** (or equivalent TOEFL / IB English / A-Level English). This is one of the lowest English thresholds among Hong Kong tertiary institutions, reflecting the conservatoire model where studio teaching often happens in Cantonese or Putonghua.

### Audition, portfolio and interview - the deciding factor

Every HKAPA applicant goes through a **discipline-specific selection process** decided by their target School:

| School | Typical selection format |
| --- | --- |
| Chinese Opera | Performance audition (singing, recitation, body movement, percussion piece) + interview |
| Dance | Technique class + solo in chosen major (Ballet / Chinese / Contemporary) + improvisation + interview |
| Drama | Two contrasting monologues (one classical, one contemporary), movement / voice work, group improvisation, interview |
| Film and Television | Portfolio submission (showreel, screenplay, photography, design folio per stream) + entry test + interview |
| Music | Pre-screening video + live audition on principal instrument / voice + sight-reading + ear test + theory test + interview |
| Theatre and Entertainment Arts | Portfolio (drawings, technical drafts, design boards, model boxes, photographs of past production work) + interview |

For 2026 entry, **non-local applicants** unable to travel may submit a high-quality digital recording / portfolio in lieu of in-person audition, but HKAPA strongly recommends attending in person where feasible. The **second-round Dance audition for 2026 entry** is scheduled for **24-25 January 2026**.

### Application timeline

- **Application opens**: typically September of the year before entry
- **Main round closing**: typically late November / early December
- **Late round (subject to programme availability)**: until June
- **Auditions / interviews**: November - April (some Schools run multiple rounds)
- **Offers**: rolling, with most offers by April / May

## 4. Tuition fees and scholarships (2026/27 reference)

### Tuition

HKAPA tuition is structured by funded vs non-funded seats:

- **Local (Hong Kong) students - UGC-funded seats**: **HK$44,500 per year**, the same as the Big 8 UGC undergraduate fee
- **Non-local students** (mainland China and overseas): typically **HK$140,000 - HK$180,000 per year** depending on programme (broadly USD 18,000 - 23,000), comparable to the lower end of Big 8 non-local fees

Postgraduate Diploma, Diploma and Advanced Diploma programmes have separate fee schedules - generally lower than the Bachelor's level.

### Living costs

A realistic Hong Kong undergraduate budget remains **HK$70,000 - HK$120,000 per year** for accommodation, food, transport and personal items. HKAPA does not operate a traditional residential hall system on the same scale as the Big 8; many non-local students rent private accommodation in Wan Chai, North Point or eastern Hong Kong Island, where the campus is highly accessible. HKAPA does maintain a non-local student hostel and provides housing assistance.

### Scholarships

- **HKSAR Government Scholarship Fund**: open to outstanding local and non-local students; awards range from partial tuition to full tuition coverage
- **The Society of APA Scholarships**: awarded annually to students of high artistic achievement
- **Belt and Road Scholarship**: for students from designated Belt and Road countries
- **Targeted Scholarships for non-local students** from mainland China and selected overseas territories
- **Hundreds of named scholarships and prizes** funded by donors and industry partners (Cathay, Swire, HSBC, Disney, Cha Family Foundation, Tung Foundation, etc.) - HKAPA disburses tens of millions of HKD in financial support each year, and high-talent admits routinely receive scholarship offers attached to their admission letter

## 5. Flagship programmes worth a closer look

### Bachelor of Fine Arts (Honours) in Theatre and Entertainment Arts (TEA)

Arguably HKAPA's most internationally recruited degree. Production stream graduates work as stage managers, lighting and sound designers, set and costume designers, technical directors, and event producers across Hong Kong, mainland China, Singapore, Macau (theme parks) and increasingly the Middle East live entertainment sector. Cohort sizes are small (15-25 per stream), and final-year capstone productions are mounted on HKAPA's professional stages with full crews.

### Bachelor of Music (Honours)

HKAPA's BMus is the leading conservatoire degree in Hong Kong. The Chinese Music stream is particularly distinctive - one of the few degree-level Chinese instrumental performance pathways in the world, with direct artistic links to the Hong Kong Chinese Orchestra. Western strings, woodwinds, brass and piano students benefit from masterclasses with visiting Hong Kong Philharmonic principals and international guest artists.

### Bachelor of Fine Arts (Honours) in Drama

Strong record placing alumni in Hong Kong's professional theatre scene (Hong Kong Repertory Theatre, Chung Ying Theatre, Tang Shu-wing Theatre Studio) and into Cantonese-language film and TVB drama. Acting alumni include household-name film and TV actors and stage directors.

### Bachelor of Fine Arts (Honours) in Cinema and Television

Practice-led training in directing, cinematography, producing, screenwriting, editing, sound and production design. Hong Kong's commercial film industry continues to recruit cinematographers, gaffers, focus pullers, editors and production designers directly from this programme. The Béthanie campus and HKAPA's industry placements are key advantages.

### Bachelor of Fine Arts (Honours) in Dance

Streams in Ballet, Chinese Dance and Contemporary Dance. Graduates feed into Hong Kong Ballet, City Contemporary Dance Company, Hong Kong Dance Company, and increasingly into mainland and overseas companies (Cloud Gate, Beijing Dance Theatre, contemporary ensembles in Europe).

### Bachelor of Fine Arts (Honours) in Chinese Opera

The only conservatoire-level Cantonese opera Bachelor's degree in the world. Funded by both HKAPA and Hong Kong's Cantonese Opera Development Fund. Graduates form the backbone of Hong Kong's opera principal pipeline.

## 6. Graduate outcomes

Because HKAPA's mission is professional vocational training, its employment outcomes are best read **by industry**, not by salary tables.

- **Theatre and Entertainment Arts**: very high industry employment (often >95%) within six months. Lighting, sound and stage management graduates are consistently in short supply in the Hong Kong, Macau, Singapore and Middle East live entertainment markets
- **Music**: graduates take orchestral seats, build studio teaching practices, take up positions with Hong Kong Philharmonic, Hong Kong Sinfonietta, Hong Kong Chinese Orchestra, the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts itself, or proceed to international postgraduate programmes (Royal Academy / Royal College / Juilliard / Curtis / Eastman / Berklee, etc.)
- **Drama**: a mix of professional theatre, TV, film and voiceover work; many alumni join Hong Kong Repertory Theatre and Chung Ying Theatre
- **Film and Television**: direct entry into Hong Kong film, drama, advertising and streaming production crews; alumni regularly nominated at the Hong Kong Film Awards, Golden Horse and Fresh Wave
- **Dance**: contracts with Hong Kong Ballet, CCDC, HKDC and overseas companies; many alumni teach in Hong Kong dance studios and international schools
- **Chinese Opera**: principal and supporting roles with Hong Kong's professional Cantonese opera houses

HKAPA graduates are also eligible for the Immigration Department's **IANG (Immigration Arrangements for Non-local Graduates)** scheme on the same terms as Big 8 graduates - 24 months of unconditional stay-and-work post-graduation - and may apply for **Hong Kong permanent residence after seven years** of ordinary residence.

## 7. Should HKAPA be on your list?

HKAPA is the right choice if **at least three** of the following apply to you:

1. Your strongest profile is artistic, performance-based or technical-craft, not academic
2. You can present a serious audition, portfolio or showreel demonstrating real promise in your chosen discipline
3. You want a small, hands-on conservatoire environment and direct mentorship from working industry professionals
4. You are willing to live and work in Cantonese, Putonghua and English studio environments
5. You see your career as a performer, designer, technician or producer in performing arts, film or live entertainment - not in finance, law, medicine or general business

If your priority is a broad, conventional university experience with classmates across many disciplines, the Big 8 will suit you better. If your priority is **becoming an artist or performing arts professional in Asia**, HKAPA is, on the strength of its 2026 QS performing arts ranking, faculty pedigree and direct industry pipeline, the strongest single choice on the Hong Kong map - and one of the strongest in the world.

## 8. Practical next steps

1. **Identify your target School and stream early.** Each School has its own audition requirement and timeline. Do not generalise.
2. **Build your audition / portfolio over months, not weeks.** Strong HKAPA admits typically prepare 6-12 months in advance with a teacher, mentor or coach.
3. **Watch HKAPA productions.** Public performances at the Wan Chai campus (most are open to the public, many free or low-cost) are the single best way to feel whether the Academy fits you.
4. **Submit early.** Applications open in September; early applicants get the widest audition slot choice and the best chance at scholarship consideration.
5. **Have an academic backup.** Even strong artistic candidates should keep a JUPAS application open for the Big 8, and consider arts management or related programmes at PolyU, BU, EdUHK or self-financing institutions as alternatives if the audition does not go your way.

For the most current 2026/27 deadlines, fee schedule and audition dates, always cross-check the official HKAPA admissions pages at **hkapa.edu** before submitting your application.

# Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU) Complete Guide 2026

Among Hong Kong's eight UGC-funded universities, Hong Kong Baptist University — HKBU, or simply BU as students call it — does not try to compete with HKU, CUHK and HKUST on overall research firepower. Instead, it has spent the last three decades building unrivalled depth in three quite specific areas: **Communication and Media Studies (the leading school of its kind in Asia)**, **Chinese Medicine (the first Hong Kong university to offer a Bachelor of Chinese Medicine)**, and **Creative Arts (a 2022-formed academy that consolidates film, music and visual arts under one roof)**.

If you are a DSE candidate or an international applicant whose interests lie in journalism and broadcasting, film and music production, visual arts, Chinese medicine, applied data science, or social sciences with a strong humanities flavour, HKBU offers something its larger peers cannot: small classes, an intimate campus in the heart of Kowloon Tong, and faculties that are global leaders in their narrow specialisms rather than middle-of-the-pack contributors to a giant comprehensive university. With only around 5,800 undergraduates, the student-to-faculty ratio sits near 1:14, and signature programmes such as Journalism, Film & Television, and Music routinely run in classes of 15–25.

This guide covers the 2026/27 admissions cycle: the QS rankings story, the eight faculties, the JUPAS and non-JUPAS application routes, tuition fees and scholarships, the flagship programmes you should know about, and what graduates actually do after they leave the Kowloon Tong campus.

---

## 1. What kind of university is HKBU?

HKBU was founded in **1956** as Hong Kong Baptist College and gained full university status in **1994**, making it the **second-oldest higher education institution in Hong Kong** after HKU. Its main campus sits on Waterloo Road and Renfrew Road in **Kowloon Tong**, directly served by the MTR Kwun Tong Line and East Rail Line interchange — Festival Walk shopping mall is across the street, and Central is roughly 30 minutes away by metro. Among the eight UGC-funded universities, HKBU's location is one of the most convenient.

The "Baptist" in the name reflects the institution's founding by the Baptist Convention of Hong Kong in the 1950s, but HKBU today operates as a fully secular public research university. There is no religious requirement at admission, and Christianity-related courses appear only as electives within the General Education programme. The motto, **"Truth and Service"** (篤信力行), has remained unchanged since the college era.

### Size and campus character

- Around **5,800 undergraduates** and **5,000 postgraduates**, total enrolment of about 11,000 — one of the smallest among the eight UGC-funded universities
- **Student-to-faculty ratio of approximately 1:14**, with small-class teaching the norm in Communication, Creative Arts and Chinese Medicine programmes
- Operates **Hong Kong's most fully equipped university broadcasting and recording facilities**, attached to the School of Communication
- The campus is **physically compact** — the entire main and Shaw campuses can be walked end-to-end in under fifteen minutes
- A **secondary campus** for Creative Arts and Chinese Medicine sits a short walk away in the Ho Sin Hang Campus and the Kai Tak development is hosting the new School of Chinese Medicine teaching hospital opening in phases through 2026 and 2027

The campus's small size is a real advantage for incoming students: you bump into your classmates, your professors and the campus restaurants in the same buildings every day. It is the closest thing in Hong Kong to a liberal-arts-college feel attached to a research university.

---

## 2. HKBU's place in 2026 rankings

The 2026 ranking cycle is the strongest year HKBU has had in roughly a decade.

| Ranking | 2026 result | Movement |
|---|---|---|
| QS World University Rankings 2026 | #=244 globally | Continued steady climb |
| QS Asia University Rankings 2026 | **#53 in Asia** | Jumped from #71 in 2025 — best result since 2016 |
| Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2026 | 351–400 band | Stable |
| THE Impact Rankings 2025 — Quality Education (SDG 4) | **#2 globally** | A signature result |

The 18-place jump in the QS Asia rankings is HKBU's most important headline this year. The university attributes the move to improvements in academic reputation, employer reputation, and international research network indicators. For applicants, the practical reading is: HKBU is no longer the smallest of the eight UGC universities by reputation. It now sits comfortably above several mainland Chinese 985 universities on the QS Asia table.

### Subject rankings worth knowing

- **Communication & Media Studies** — QS world top 51–100, the strongest position of any HKBU subject and a long-standing leader within Asia
- **Hospitality & Leisure Management, Performing Arts, Linguistics, Religious Studies, Business & Management** — all in the QS world top 200–400 range
- **Mathematics and Computer Science** — rising in 2026 thanks to investment in the Department of Computer Science and the new BSc in AI

The takeaway: HKBU's prestige is concentrated, not spread thin. If your target subject is on the strong list, the university is genuinely competitive with anything in the region.

---

## 3. The eight faculties and what they offer

HKBU restructured its undergraduate offering in 2022/23, splitting the historic Faculty of Social Sciences from the Faculty of Arts and giving the Academy of Visual Arts, the Academy of Film and the Department of Music a unified home as the **School of Creative Arts**. The 2026/27 structure is:

1. **Faculty of Arts** — English Language and Literature, Translation, Humanities, History, Religious Studies and Philosophy, plus Chinese Language and Literature
2. **Faculty of Social Sciences** — Sociology, Government and International Studies, Geography, Social Work, Education Studies and Sport Studies
3. **Faculty of Science** — Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Statistics, Environment Science, Applied Biology, and a flagship undergraduate AI programme launched in 2024
4. **School of Business** — Accountancy, Economics, Finance, Marketing, Information Systems and Business Administration; AACSB- and EQUIS-accredited
5. **School of Communication** — Journalism, Public Relations and Advertising, Film, Television and Digital Visual Production; the historical core of the university's reputation
6. **School of Chinese Medicine** — Bachelor of Chinese Medicine and Bachelor of Science (Hons) in Biomedical Science (six-year combined programme), the first such offering at any Hong Kong university
7. **School of Creative Arts** — three academies under one school: the Academy of Film, the Department of Music and the Academy of Visual Arts
8. **Division of Transdisciplinary Studies** — bridge programmes such as Media Arts, Sustainability Management and AI and Social Innovation

The university advertises **22 admission programmes leading to more than 45 majors**, with a broad-based admission model that lets DSE students start in a faculty and declare a final major after their first year.

---

## 4. Flagship programmes you should know about

### School of Communication — Asia's leading communications school

The School of Communication is the single best-known unit at HKBU and the reason most international applicants put the university on their list. Its three undergraduate departments — **Journalism**, **Communication Studies** (Public Relations, Advertising, Organisational Communication), and **Film, Television and Digital Visual Production** — share one of the largest university-owned television studios, radio stations and recording facilities in the region.

- Journalism graduates routinely fill the editorial benches of South China Morning Post, RTHK, Hong Kong Free Press, Bloomberg HK, Reuters HK and a long list of mainland and international outlets
- The Film Academy has produced a disproportionate share of Hong Kong's working art-house and commercial directors over the last two decades
- The school's broadcast facilities are used for live student news bulletins and for a substantial volume of professional production work

JUPAS competition for Communication is among the highest at HKBU — admission scores typically sit at the upper end of the university's range.

### School of Chinese Medicine — Hong Kong's first BCM

HKBU's School of Chinese Medicine offers a **six-year combined Bachelor of Chinese Medicine and Bachelor of Science (Hons) in Biomedical Science** programme. It was the first programme of its kind anywhere in Hong Kong, and it is still the school most applicants think of when they consider Chinese medicine as a career. Graduates qualify to sit the Hong Kong Chinese Medicine Practitioners Licensing Examination and to practise across the territory and increasingly in the Greater Bay Area.

A new Chinese Medicine teaching hospital adjacent to the Kai Tak development is being commissioned in phases — the first major dedicated CM hospital in Hong Kong — and HKBU's school is the principal academic partner.

### School of Creative Arts — film, music and visual arts under one roof

Formed in 2022, the School of Creative Arts is HKBU's newest school but its constituent academies are decades old. The **Academy of Film** trains directors, screenwriters and producers; the **Department of Music** teaches Western classical performance, composition and music technology; and the **Academy of Visual Arts**, located on the historic Kai Tak Campus, is the territory's leading studio-based fine arts programme.

For a creative-arts applicant who wants a serious portfolio-based undergraduate education in Hong Kong, this is the most concentrated option in the city.

### School of Business — small but accredited

HKBU's School of Business is the smallest of the four AACSB+EQUIS double-accredited business schools in the eight-university system, but the small size translates into a high level of personal attention. Its **BBA in Global Business Management**, **BBA in Accounting**, and **BBA in Finance** routinely place graduates into Big Four audit roles, mid-tier investment banks and the Greater Bay Area corporate sector.

### Faculty of Science — AI and Data Science as new flagships

The most significant academic investment of the past three years has been the expansion of the Department of Computer Science and the launch of a dedicated **BSc in Artificial Intelligence** programme in 2024. Graduates of the new AI track are competing successfully for places in mainland tech firms, Hong Kong fintech roles, and overseas master's programmes.

---

## 5. Admission routes and entrance requirements 2026/27

HKBU recruits undergraduates through three main routes.

### Route A — JUPAS (HKDSE candidates)

The general entrance requirements (GER) for 2026 entry to a JUPAS programme require:

- **Four core subjects**: Chinese Language Level 3, English Language Level 3, Mathematics (Compulsory Part) Level 2, and Citizenship and Social Development "Attained"
- **Two elective subjects** at Level 3 or above (or equivalent, with M1/M2 mathematics and Other Language Subjects accepted)

Programme-specific entrance requirements (PER) sit on top of GER and vary widely. Communication, Chinese Medicine, the BBA suite and Computer Science have higher PERs than the university floor; some Faculty of Arts and Sport and Recreation Leadership programmes admit at GER. The 2025 admissions data shows **median Best 5 scores ranging from the upper teens to the mid-twenties** depending on programme.

Application is via the central JUPAS system. Bands and choice ordering follow the standard JUPAS rules — for HKBU, putting target programmes in Band A is essential for the most competitive seats.

### Route B — Non-JUPAS direct admission (international and mainland China applicants)

Applicants holding qualifications other than HKDSE — Gaokao, A-Level, IB, SAT/ACT, or recognised international school diplomas — apply directly to HKBU via the Online Application System.

For 2026/27 entry:

- **Mainland Gaokao**: HKBU is one of the eight UGC-funded universities recruiting on Gaokao scores via direct application (not via the central mainland 提前批 channel for HKBU). The university typically requires a score above the **Tier 1 (一本/特殊类型) line by 80–120 points** depending on programme, with English at **120 or above** for most programmes and **130 or above** for Communication, Translation and English Language and Literature. An admissions interview (in person or video) is standard
- **A-Level / IAL**: Three A2 passes, typically AAA–ABB depending on programme; specific science passes for Chinese Medicine and Science programmes
- **IB Diploma**: 30–38 points depending on programme, with HL subject requirements
- **SAT / ACT**: SAT 1300+ or ACT 28+ as a baseline, plus four AP scores or a US high school diploma

The application window for 2026/27 entry runs from **November 2025 to early January 2026** for the main round, with rolling admission for some programmes through to mid-year.

### Route C — Direct Admission Schemes (HKDSE candidates outside JUPAS)

A subset of HKDSE candidates — those holding additional international qualifications, or applying to Sport and Recreation Leadership, Music, Visual Arts or Film with strong portfolios — can apply through HKBU's Direct Admission Schemes. Acceptances under these schemes are conditional on meeting HKDSE benchmarks but allow earlier offers and reduce reliance on JUPAS band ordering.

---

## 6. Tuition fees, scholarships and total cost

### Local tuition (UGC-funded, HKDSE)

The standard UGC-funded undergraduate tuition fee for local students in 2026/27 is **HK$44,500 per year**. Local students with financial need can apply for the Tertiary Student Finance Scheme (TSFS) and Non-means-tested Loan Scheme (NLSPS) administered by the Hong Kong Working Family and Student Financial Assistance Agency.

### Non-local tuition

For 2026/27 entry, HKBU sets its non-local undergraduate tuition at:

- **General undergraduate programmes: HK$145,000 per year** — among the more affordable rates among the eight UGC-funded universities
- The university has confirmed tuition rises in line with sector trends but at the lower end of the band among the eight universities

### Living costs

For a non-local student living on or near the Kowloon Tong campus:

- **Hostel (on-campus, contested allocation)**: HK$10,000–18,000 per year
- **Off-campus rental in Kowloon Tong / Sham Shui Po / Mong Kok**: HK$6,000–10,000 per month for a shared room, HK$10,000–15,000 for a studio
- **Food**: HK$3,000–5,000 per month if you mostly eat on campus and at neighbourhood cha chaan tengs
- **All-in annual living budget**: HK$80,000–130,000

A non-local student should budget around **HK$220,000–280,000 per year all-in**, depending on accommodation choices. Over four years, that translates to roughly **HK$900,000–1,100,000** for a full undergraduate education.

### Scholarships

HKBU has expanded its entrance scholarship pool considerably in the last two cycles to attract top-band applicants:

- **HKBU Entrance Scholarship for Non-local Students** — full-tuition or half-tuition awards for outstanding Gaokao, A-Level and IB applicants
- **President's Scholarship** — full tuition plus an annual stipend for the top 1–2% of incoming students
- **School of Business Admission Scholarships** — HK$60,000 to full-tuition awards for top-band BBA applicants
- **Faculty-specific scholarships** in Communication, Chinese Medicine and Creative Arts

Mainland Gaokao applicants scoring in the top 0.5% of their province routinely receive at least a half-tuition award.

---

## 7. Hostel and student life

HKBU's two on-campus halls — **N.T. Wong Hall** and **Wing Lung Bank Hall** — house roughly 1,800 students between them. With around 5,800 undergraduates, the on-campus hall guarantee covers **first-year non-locals and a competitive scoring system** for upper-year students. Most non-local students will spend at least two of their four undergraduate years in private rental in Kowloon Tong, Sham Shui Po, Mong Kok or Tai Kok Tsui — all within 20 minutes of campus by MTR or bus.

The hostel culture is more low-key than at HKU or CUHK. There is a hall-life society, but the student union and academic society scenes — particularly the Communication Students' Association (傳播系學會) and the Film Academy student society — are more active.

The 9-month term structure mirrors the rest of the eight UGC-funded universities: Term 1 from early September to mid-December, Term 2 from mid-January to early May, with an optional summer term in June and July.

---

## 8. Graduate outcomes

The 2024 Joint University Programmes Admissions Council survey reports HKBU graduate average starting salaries in the **HK$22,000–28,000 per month** band overall, with significant variance by programme:

- **School of Business**: HK$25,000–32,000 starting; Big Four and mid-tier investment bank placements remain strong
- **School of Communication**: HK$20,000–26,000 starting in journalism and PR; higher in advertising and digital production
- **School of Chinese Medicine**: HK$30,000–40,000 once licensed and practising, with substantial demand from public CM clinics and the new Kai Tak teaching hospital
- **School of Creative Arts**: more variable — film and music graduates often go freelance or into postgraduate study; visual arts graduates increasingly find stable roles in art education and gallery work
- **Faculty of Science (AI track)**: HK$24,000–30,000 starting; competitive with Computer Science cohorts at the larger universities

A meaningful share of HKBU graduates go on to **postgraduate study at HKU, CUHK, mainland C9 universities or overseas Russell Group / Ivy-Plus institutions**. The university's small size means that a strong undergraduate transcript is well-known to faculty members writing references.

---

## 9. Who should apply to HKBU?

You should put HKBU near the top of your list if:

- You want **journalism, film, television, advertising, public relations or visual arts**, and you want a school with the deepest concentration of these programmes in Asia
- You want to study **Chinese medicine** at the only six-year integrated BCM-Biomedical Science programme in the city, with a brand-new teaching hospital coming online
- You want a **smaller, more personal undergraduate experience** with class sizes in the teens and twenties, in a campus that feels like a single community rather than a city
- Your DSE Best 5 sits in the upper teens to mid-twenties, and you want a programme where this score reaches Band A choices for competitive majors rather than the safety options at the larger universities
- You are a Gaokao applicant scoring 80–120 points above the Tier 1 line with strong English, and you want a Hong Kong UGC-funded university that offers tuition at the lower end of the non-local fee band

If your priority is global comprehensive ranking — engineering, medicine, hard sciences in the QS world top 100 — HKU, CUHK, HKUST, PolyU and CityU sit ahead of HKBU on most tables. But if any of the specialist domains above match your interests, HKBU's depth in those subjects is on a different scale from its size.

---

## 10. Application checklist for 2026/27

- [ ] Decide your route: JUPAS, Non-JUPAS direct, or Direct Admission Schemes
- [ ] Confirm GER and PER on the HKBU Undergraduate Admissions site for each target programme
- [ ] For Communication, Creative Arts and Music, prepare a portfolio or audition tape early — many accept submissions from October
- [ ] For non-JUPAS, register on the HKBU Online Application System and submit before the **early January 2026** deadline
- [ ] For Gaokao applicants, monitor provincial cutoff publication in late June 2026 and submit Gaokao results to HKBU as soon as they are released
- [ ] Apply for entrance scholarships — most require the same application form and a brief personal statement
- [ ] Apply for the on-campus hostel via the Office of Student Affairs once you have an offer
- [ ] If applying for a student visa, begin the IANG / 學生簽證 process via the Hong Kong Immigration Department as soon as the offer letter arrives — the process takes 6–8 weeks

HKBU's admission cycle is one of the more responsive in the eight UGC system, and the international admissions team typically replies to direct queries within a few business days during the application window. For DSE candidates, JUPAS rules and timing apply as standard; for everyone else, **apply early** — the most competitive Communication, Chinese Medicine and Creative Arts programmes fill in the first two rounds.
