# Hong Kong Physiotherapy Bachelor (PolyU JS3636) Complete Guide 2026

In Hong Kong, "physiotherapist" is a regulated allied health title carrying social standing, pay and job security comparable to many medical specialties. To practise legally, a graduate must register with the **Physiotherapists Board of Hong Kong** under the Supplementary Medical Professions Ordinance (Cap. 359). The fastest and most direct undergraduate route to that licence is a single programme: **The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) Department of Rehabilitation Sciences, JS3636 Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Physiotherapy**. Together with Occupational Therapy and Medical Imaging, Physiotherapy is one of "PolyU's three treasures" - perennially among the highest-scoring, most competitive non-medical undergraduate offers in the city.

This guide is written for 2026 entrants and prospective DSE, Non-JUPAS and Mainland Gaokao applicants. It walks through curriculum structure, admission requirements, clinical placements, professional registration, graduate destinations and salary scales, with practical notes on subject choice and interview preparation.

## 1. Why PolyU Physiotherapy? Hong Kong's only direct registration pathway

Under Cap. 359, no person in Hong Kong may use the title "physiotherapist" or practise independently without registration with the Physiotherapists Board. For decades, the only locally-trained, full-time undergraduate qualification recognised for direct registration has been **PolyU JS3636**. Hong Kong Metropolitan University (HKMU) and the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) have launched or planned new undergraduate physiotherapy programmes in recent years, but PolyU remains the long-established institution whose degree is fully recognised by **World Physiotherapy** (formerly WCPT) and whose graduates qualify for Hong Kong registration **without sitting Part I/Part II licensure examinations**.

Direct registration is the headline benefit. After completing the BSc (Hons) and the minimum 1,000 hours of supervised clinical practice required by the Board, PolyU graduates apply to the Physiotherapists Board and receive their Registered Physiotherapist (RPT) status through documentary review alone. Holders of overseas physiotherapy degrees, by contrast, must submit their qualifications for assessment and most are required to pass a written examination and a clinical competency assessment before registration is granted.

## 2. Programme structure: four years, 132 credits, 17% clinical

### 2.1 Basics

- **JUPAS code**: JS3636
- **Duration**: 4 years, full-time
- **Total credits**: 132 (approximately 23 of which are clinical/fieldwork credits)
- **Department**: Rehabilitation Sciences, within the Faculty of Health and Social Sciences
- **Entry**: September 2026
- **Intake**: 150 students per cohort (combined JUPAS and Non-JUPAS), making it one of the smaller and more selective allied health intakes in Hong Kong
- **Funding status**: Government-funded (UGC)
- **Award**: BSc (Hons) in Physiotherapy

### 2.2 Curriculum spine

The four-year curriculum is built on a science-led foundation followed by progressive clinical specialisation:

- **Year 1** - Anatomy, physiology, biomechanics, kinesiology, foundational behavioural sciences and an introduction to physiotherapy practice. Students also complete University Core, GUR (General University Requirements) including Service Learning, Chinese, English and Healthy Lifestyle components.
- **Year 2** - Pathology, exercise physiology, electrophysical agents, manual therapy, musculoskeletal and cardiopulmonary physiotherapy basics, evidence-based practice. The first short hospital observations begin.
- **Year 3** - Neurological physiotherapy, paediatric physiotherapy, women's health, sports physiotherapy, geriatric rehabilitation. Block clinical placements alternate with academic blocks. Students are expected to begin a Capstone or Honours research project.
- **Year 4** - Advanced clinical practice, professional ethics and management, capstone project completion, and intensive clinical internship rotations across acute, sub-acute, community and outpatient settings.

### 2.3 Clinical placements: 1,000+ hours across nine specialty areas

Clinical hours are the spine of the programme, and the Physiotherapists Board requires at least **1,000 hours** of supervised practice for registration. Placements rotate through the major Hospital Authority clusters (Queen Mary, Prince of Wales, Pamela Youde, United Christian, Princess Margaret and others), private rehabilitation centres, sports institutes and community settings such as elderly care homes and special schools. Placements cover at least nine specialty areas: musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiopulmonary, paediatrics, geriatrics, sports, women's health, ICU/acute care and community/primary care.

In Years 3 and 4, eligible students may apply for an optional **5-week international clinical placement**. Past destinations have included Australia, Canada, Denmark, Finland, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and the USA. Spaces are limited and selection is competitive based on GPA and clinical performance.

## 3. JUPAS admission: subject weighting and scoring

### 3.1 No compulsory science, but science weighting is real

The programme has **no compulsory subject** beyond the standard 4C+2X profile (Chinese, English, Mathematics, Citizenship & Social Development at Level 2/Attained, plus two electives). However, the admission score formula heavily favours science:

- **Best 5 subjects + 1 bonus**, with strict subject weighting
- **Higher weighting** for English, Mathematics (Compulsory or Extended Module M1/M2), Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Combined Science (with Biology/Physics components)
- **Standard weighting** for Chinese and other electives
- Citizenship & Social Development is not counted in the best-5

Most successful candidates take **Biology + Chemistry** as their core electives, with Physics or M1/M2 as the third X. A Combined Science (Biology + Physics) profile is acceptable but tends to produce a slightly lower score because it is treated as a single subject in the best-5 calculation.

### 3.2 Indicative admission scores (HKDSE 7-level)

Based on the most recently published JUPAS admission figures, JS3636 sits firmly inside the top tier of allied-health programmes:

- **Median best-5 + weighting score**: approximately 31-32 points (close to 5*5*5*5*5 territory)
- **Lower quartile**: around 30 points
- **Upper quartile**: around 33 points
- Conversion to PolyU's own weighted scale typically falls in the **215-220 range**, broadly in line with second-batch Medicine programmes and ahead of most non-medical professional degrees

In practice, candidates aiming at JS3636 plan for an "almost-medicine" academic profile: 5* in core subjects, 5 minimum in two science electives, and a strong English score (Level 5 or above) to clear interview shortlisting comfortably.

### 3.3 Interview

Shortlisted candidates are invited to a **group or individual interview**, usually held in May-June after the JUPAS application close. The interview assesses:

- Communication skills in English (and sometimes Cantonese)
- Awareness of the physiotherapist's scope of practice and the differences from doctors, occupational therapists and chiropractors
- Ethical reasoning - typical scenarios involve elderly patients, paediatric cases or refusal of treatment
- Commitment to a healthcare career and physical readiness for a clinically demanding profession

Interview performance does not replace the academic score but is used to break ties among candidates with similar DSE results. A weak interview can move a borderline candidate down to the waiting list.

## 4. Non-JUPAS, international and Mainland Gaokao routes

### 4.1 Non-JUPAS Year 1 entry

Non-JUPAS Year 1 entry is open to applicants holding GCE A-Level, IB Diploma, SAT/AP, or other recognised qualifications. Indicative requirements:

- **GCE A-Level**: typically AAA in three subjects, including at least one of Biology, Chemistry, Physics
- **IB Diploma**: 38-42 points, including HL Biology or Chemistry at 6 or 7
- **SAT**: 1380+ (Evidence-Based Reading & Writing, Math) plus AP scores of 4-5 in two relevant subjects
- **English**: IELTS 6.5 (no sub-score below 6.0) or TOEFL iBT 80, unless the qualification is taught and examined in English
- **Application deadline**: typically 5 February of the entry year

### 4.2 Mainland Gaokao route

PolyU operates outside the Mainland Mass Enrolment Scheme and recruits Gaokao candidates through its own **Mainland Direct Admissions** track. For physiotherapy:

- **Gaokao total score**: well above the local first-tier (一本/特殊类型) line, typically equivalent to top-30 Mainland university level
- **English subscore**: 130/150 or higher
- Subject preference: science track (理科/物理类) with strong Biology and Physics
- Interview: required, usually conducted in English with some Cantonese

### 4.3 International applicants

International applicants apply through PolyU's International Admissions portal with a deadline of around mid-May. The same English thresholds apply, plus a clinical-practice readiness check (no relevant communicable disease restrictions, ability to cope with physical workload).

## 5. Tuition, scholarships and total cost

- **UGC tuition (local students)**: HK$44,500 per academic year
- **Non-local tuition**: HK$170,000-180,000 per academic year (for 2026 entry; refer to PolyU's official figures for the latest)
- **Hostel** (limited, allocated by points): HK$15,000-22,000 per year
- **Off-campus housing in Hung Hom / Ho Man Tin**: HK$6,000-10,000 per month for a shared flat
- **Books, uniform, lab consumables**: HK$3,000-5,000 per year; clinical placements require a uniform set, name badge and a stethoscope/goniometer kit
- **Insurance**: PolyU clinical placements require professional indemnity coverage, included via student membership of the Hong Kong Physiotherapy Association

Major scholarships include the HKSAR Government Scholarship, PolyU Talent Award, Reaching Out Award (for international placements) and various Hospital Authority bonded scholarships that subsidise tuition in exchange for a service commitment after graduation.

## 6. Registration and the pathway to practise

After graduation, the registration steps are:

1. **Apply for full registration** with the Physiotherapists Board of Hong Kong (Supplementary Medical Professions Council)
2. Submit transcripts confirming completion of the BSc (Hons) and 1,000 hours of supervised clinical practice
3. Pay the registration fee and provide certificate of good standing if applicable
4. Receive Registered Physiotherapist (RPT) status, valid subject to renewal and Continuing Professional Development (CPD) requirements

Most graduates begin work as **Physiotherapist II** in the Hospital Authority, in private hospitals, or in NGO/community settings. A growing minority go straight into private practice or sports/performance settings, often with a dual qualification in dry needling, manual therapy or sports rehabilitation.

## 7. Salary, career progression and overseas mobility

### 7.1 Hospital Authority pay scale

- **Physiotherapist II (entry)**: starting salary on Master Pay Scale (MPS) Point 16, approximately **HK$36,000-39,000 per month**, with annual increments
- **Physiotherapist I**: typically reached after 5-8 years, MPS 25 onward, **HK$55,000-65,000 per month**
- **Senior Physiotherapist**: department head or specialty lead, **HK$80,000-100,000+ per month**
- 13th-month pay, housing allowance, government pension contribution (or MPF) and continuing education leave are standard benefits

### 7.2 Private sector

Private hospitals and clinics offer base salaries roughly comparable to the HA, with bonus structures based on clinical caseload. Sports physiotherapists embedded with professional teams or elite training centres can earn HK$60,000-100,000+ per month with performance incentives. A self-employed physiotherapist running a Hung Hom or Central clinic with three to five years of experience often grosses HK$100,000+ per month, before rent and overheads.

### 7.3 Overseas mobility

Because PolyU's degree is recognised by World Physiotherapy, graduates are well-placed to register in Australia (via APC), the UK (HCPC), Canada (PCC after the PCE) and Singapore (AHPC). Each jurisdiction may require a written and/or clinical exam, but PolyU's curriculum maps closely to international competency standards, and a meaningful share of each cohort emigrates within five to ten years of graduation.

## 8. Choosing physiotherapy: who should apply

JS3636 is well suited to applicants who:

- Have a strong, sustained interest in human anatomy, movement and rehabilitation
- Are physically active and comfortable with hands-on, full-body patient contact
- Communicate clearly in both Cantonese and English (the patient mix is bilingual, often with Mandarin and other dialects too)
- Can sustain a clinically intense schedule from Year 2 onwards
- Want a healthcare career with **direct patient impact, professional autonomy and predictable hours** without the length and intensity of a medical degree

Applicants who are uncertain between Medicine, Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy should shadow a working physiotherapist before committing - the day-to-day work of a physiotherapist is physical, repetitive and deeply collaborative, and the right "fit" is more important than chasing the highest-scoring offer.

## 9. Practical timeline for a 2026 applicant

- **Now to October 2025**: Lock in best-5 subject combination (target Biology, Chemistry plus one of Physics/M1/M2/Economics)
- **December 2025**: Submit JUPAS application with JS3636 in Band A, position 1 or 2
- **April 2026**: HKDSE examinations
- **May-June 2026**: Interview if shortlisted
- **Mid-July 2026**: HKDSE results release; JUPAS post-results modification within 24 hours
- **Early August 2026**: Main round JUPAS offer
- **September 2026**: Programme commencement, white-coat ceremony, first anatomy labs

PolyU JS3636 is a high-stakes, high-reward target: the bar is steep, but the destination is one of the most secure, well-respected and portable healthcare careers Hong Kong offers. For students with the academic profile and the clinical disposition, no other local programme delivers a faster route from secondary school to a Registered Physiotherapist title.

# Hong Kong Radiography Bachelor (PolyU JS3612) Complete Guide 2026

If you have set your sights on becoming a registered radiographer in Hong Kong, there is essentially one route: the Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Radiography offered by The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) under JUPAS code **JS3612**. Together with Physiotherapy (JS3636) and Occupational Therapy (JS3624), Radiography forms part of the so-called "PolyU Three Treasures" — the three allied-health degrees at PolyU that lead directly to statutory registration with a Hong Kong supplementary medical professions board, with no qualifying examination required after graduation.

This guide walks you through everything a 2026 JUPAS applicant (and their parents) needs to know: the programme structure, the choice between the Diagnostic Radiography and Radiation Therapy streams, the registration pathway through the Radiographers Board, JUPAS scoring strategy, Hospital Authority salary expectations, and where else in the world the degree is recognised.

## Why Radiography Is Worth a Serious Look

Radiographers are the imaging and radiation-treatment specialists of modern medicine. Without them, a hospital cannot run X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, mammography, fluoroscopy, nuclear medicine, or radiotherapy services. The job is technical, patient-facing, and increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence — image reconstruction, dose optimisation, lesion detection, and treatment planning are all being augmented by machine learning.

Three structural factors make this an unusually attractive field for Hong Kong students:

- **Workforce shortage.** The Hospital Authority and private hospitals have struggled to recruit enough radiographers for years. New equipment (PET-CT, MR-LINAC, robotic CT) has outpaced the supply of trained operators.
- **Aging population.** Cancer incidence rises with age, and Hong Kong's population is aging fast. Demand for both diagnostic imaging and radiation oncology will keep growing through the 2040s.
- **Single-pathway profession.** Because there is only one local accredited bachelor's programme, supply is essentially capped at PolyU's annual intake. Graduate employment outcomes are exceptionally strong.

## Programme at a Glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| JUPAS code | JS3612 |
| Full title | Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Radiography |
| Awarding institution | The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) |
| Department | Department of Health Technology and Informatics (HTI) |
| Faculty | Faculty of Health and Social Sciences |
| Duration | 4 years full-time |
| Credits | 116 academic credits + 26 clinical/field credits |
| Annual intake | ~115 students (JUPAS + Non-JUPAS combined) |
| Streams | Diagnostic Radiography (Medical Imaging) and Radiation Therapy |
| Statutory recognition | Eligible for Part II of the Register, Radiographers Board of Hong Kong |
| 2025/26 admission score (avg) | ~196.5 (Best 5 with subject weighting) |
| Entry month | September 2026 |

## The Two Streams: Diagnostic vs Radiation Therapy

A defining feature of JS3612 is that you choose a stream — usually at the end of Year 1 or beginning of Year 2 — and the curriculum diverges substantially from then on.

### Diagnostic Radiography (Medical Imaging)

This is the larger of the two streams and the one most students initially apply for. Diagnostic radiographers operate the imaging modalities that produce the pictures clinicians use to diagnose disease and guide procedures:

- **Plain radiography (X-ray)** — chest, skeletal, dental, mobile imaging in wards and theatres.
- **Computed Tomography (CT)** — cross-sectional imaging, contrast-enhanced studies, CT angiography, trauma protocols.
- **Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)** — neuro, cardiac, musculoskeletal, oncological, and functional imaging without ionising radiation.
- **Ultrasound** — increasingly performed by sonographer-radiographers in obstetric, vascular, and abdominal imaging.
- **Nuclear Medicine and PET-CT** — physiological and oncological imaging using radiopharmaceuticals.
- **Mammography and breast imaging** — screening and diagnostic.
- **Fluoroscopy and interventional radiography** — real-time imaging during cardiac catheterisation, stenting, biopsies, and theatre work.

### Radiation Therapy

The radiation therapy stream trains therapeutic radiographers (often called "RTs") who deliver radiation treatment to cancer patients, working alongside radiation oncologists and medical physicists. Core competencies include:

- **Treatment planning and dosimetry** using systems like Eclipse, RayStation, Pinnacle.
- **Patient simulation and immobilisation** using CT-Sim, MR-Sim, and PET-Sim.
- **External beam therapy** on linear accelerators, including IMRT, VMAT, SBRT, SRS, and increasingly MR-guided radiotherapy on MR-LINAC platforms.
- **Brachytherapy** for gynaecological, prostate, and head-and-neck cancers.
- **Particle therapy** principles (proton therapy is being introduced in Hong Kong's private sector).

Radiation therapists carry an enormous amount of patient-facing responsibility: they often see the same patient daily for six weeks of treatment, making strong communication skills essential. PolyU notes that **normal colour vision is not an admission requirement, but is typically required for employment in the radiation therapy sector**, and that **proficiency in Cantonese, while not an admission criterion, is in practice essential for clinical training because patients communicate in Cantonese**.

## Four-Year Curriculum Outline

The exact module list is updated annually, but the structural progression has been stable for years:

### Year 1 — Common Foundation

All students take the same modules. The goal is to build biomedical, physical, and clinical fundamentals before stream selection.

- Human Anatomy
- Human Physiology
- Introduction to Pathology
- Physics for Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy
- Radiation Science and Radiobiology
- Patient Care, Communication, and Healthcare Ethics
- General University Requirements (English, Chinese, Cluster Areas, Service Learning)

### Year 2 — Stream Differentiation Begins

Diagnostic students dive into projection radiography, CT principles, and sectional anatomy. Radiation therapy students start treatment planning principles, oncology fundamentals, and cross-sectional anatomy with a treatment focus. Both streams continue physics, instrumentation, and image processing.

### Year 3 — Advanced Modalities + First Major Clinical Placement

Diagnostic students move into MRI, ultrasound, nuclear medicine, mammography, and quality assurance. Radiation therapy students cover IMRT/VMAT, brachytherapy, paediatric and palliative oncology, and clinical dosimetry. Substantial clinical placements (in Hospital Authority hospitals such as Queen Mary, Prince of Wales, Queen Elizabeth, Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern, and Tuen Mun) are integrated into both streams.

### Year 4 — Specialisation, Research, and Capstone Placement

The final year combines an honours research project, advanced electives (paediatric imaging, interventional radiography, advanced practice in radiation therapy), and the longest clinical placement block — usually 6 to 8 months in total — to consolidate practice readiness for registration.

## Clinical Placements and Hospital Authority Partnership

Clinical training is the heart of JS3612. The 26 clinical credits represent over a thousand hours of supervised practice in real diagnostic imaging and radiation oncology departments, organised primarily through the Hospital Authority (HA) clinical training network. Students rotate through multiple HA hospitals to experience different patient populations, equipment vendors (Siemens, GE, Philips, Canon, Varian, Elekta), and clinical workflows.

Clinical placements are competency-based: students work through structured logbooks, supervised by HA radiographers and clinical instructors from PolyU. Failure to meet clinical competencies can delay graduation.

## Registration Pathway: The Radiographers Board of Hong Kong

This is what makes JS3612 different from a generic biomedical or imaging-related degree. PolyU graduates of the BSc (Hons) in Radiography are eligible to apply for **registration in Part II of the Register of the Radiographers Board of Hong Kong**, the statutory body under the Supplementary Medical Professions Council that regulates the practice of radiography in Hong Kong.

The practical implications:

1. You can be employed legally as a radiographer in Hong Kong immediately after graduation and registration. There is no separate licensing examination as there is in some other jurisdictions.
2. Without Part II registration, you cannot practise radiography in Hong Kong's public or private hospitals.
3. There is no other locally-accredited bachelor's programme that confers this eligibility. Postgraduate options exist (e.g. PolyU's MSc in Medical Imaging and Radiation Science, MMI), but they primarily serve practising radiographers seeking specialty advancement, not first-time entrants.

## JUPAS Admission Scoring

PolyU calculates a programme-specific admission score for JS3612 using the **Best 5 subjects with subject weighting**.

### Subject Requirements and Weighting

There is **no compulsory subject requirement** beyond the general PolyU entrance requirements (3322 + 33 in 4 core subjects). However, JS3612 designates a list of **preferred subjects with the highest weighting** — and given how competitive admission is, in practice you need at least two or three of these to be a serious candidate:

- Chinese Language
- English Language
- Mathematics (Compulsory Part)
- Biology
- Chemistry
- Physics
- Combined Science: Biology + Chemistry
- Combined Science: Biology + Physics
- Combined Science: Physics + Chemistry

In practice, the strongest applicants usually present **English, Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, and Physics** (or two of Bio/Chem/Phys with another preferred subject) so that all five Best-5 subjects fall into the weighted category.

### Indicative Cut-Off

The 2025/26 average admission score for JS3612 was approximately **196.5** under the Best-5-with-weighting formula. Translated to a non-weighted Best-5, this corresponds roughly to a median DSE applicant of around **5/5/5/5/5 or 5*/5/5/5/5** — broadly comparable to mid-tier business or engineering programmes at HKU or CUHK, and clearly competitive but well short of medicine or dentistry at HKU.

### Flexible Admission

PolyU operates a flexible admission scheme allowing applicants who fall short of the formal cut-off but demonstrate exceptional non-academic achievements (regional sports representation, music distinction, social service leadership, science Olympiad, etc.) to be considered. This is rarely the deciding factor for JS3612 specifically, but can help borderline candidates.

## Personal Qualities and Realistic Expectations

Beyond the score, the admissions interview probes whether you actually understand the profession. Useful self-assessment questions:

- **Are you comfortable around sick, anxious, and elderly patients, including those receiving cancer treatment?** Radiation therapists in particular form long therapeutic relationships with palliative patients.
- **Do you have the manual dexterity and spatial reasoning for positioning?** Projection radiography is surprisingly physical — patients in pain, mobile imaging in cramped wards, awkward angles.
- **Can you handle shift work and on-call?** HA radiographers work nights, weekends, and public holidays, especially in trauma centres.
- **Are you comfortable with radiation as a tool?** This sounds obvious, but some students get cold feet once they realise they will work daily with ionising radiation. The doses to staff are tightly controlled and, with proper practice, far below any harmful threshold — but the psychological adjustment is real.

## Career Outcomes and Salary

### Hospital Authority

The HA hires the majority of new graduates as **Radiographer II** on the public-sector master pay scale. Starting salary for Radiographer II is typically around **HK$36,000 to HK$45,000 per month** depending on Master Pay Scale (MPS) entry point, with annual increments. Senior Radiographer (after several years), Department Manager, and Chief Radiographer roles take you considerably higher.

Allowances on top of base salary include shift, on-call, and (for radiation therapy) special radiation allowances where applicable. Total cash compensation for a mid-career HA radiographer can exceed HK$70,000–HK$90,000 per month.

### Private Sector

Private hospitals (Hong Kong Sanatorium, Adventist, Union, Matilda, Gleneagles, CUHK Medical Centre, HKU-Shenzhen) and private imaging centres compete aggressively for HA-trained radiographers. Private-sector base pay is often **20–40% higher** than HA, especially for MRI- and CT-experienced staff, though benefits packages differ.

### Industry and Adjacent Careers

A radiography degree opens doors beyond the imaging suite:

- **Application specialists** for vendors (Siemens Healthineers, GE HealthCare, Philips, Canon Medical, Varian/Siemens, Elekta).
- **Clinical research coordinators** in radiology and oncology trials.
- **Medical imaging informatics** — PACS administration, AI integration, deep-learning model validation.
- **Postgraduate progression** into Medical Physics, Radiology MD pathway (if pursuing medicine later), Public Health, or Health Informatics.

## Overseas Recognition

PolyU radiography graduates are recognised by several major overseas registration bodies, which makes the degree unusually portable:

- **United Kingdom** — eligible to apply for Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) registration.
- **Australia** — eligible to apply for Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) / Medical Radiation Practice Board registration, typically after meeting English-language and clinical-experience requirements.
- **Singapore** — eligible for Allied Health Professions Council (AHPC) registration.
- **New Zealand** — eligible for Medical Radiation Technologists Board registration.

For most overseas registrations, **one year of post-qualification clinical experience in Hong Kong** is the practical prerequisite. A small number of graduates use this as a springboard to relocate to Australia or Canada.

## Non-JUPAS, International, and Mainland Routes

JS3612 also admits Non-JUPAS Year 1 applicants (associate-degree holders, IB, A-Level, GCE, SAT, Gaokao, and other international qualifications). Indicative benchmarks:

- **GCE A-Level** — typically AAA in three subjects including two from Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics.
- **IB Diploma** — typically 38–40 points with HL Biology/Chemistry.
- **Gaokao** — first-tier line plus interview, with strong English and a science profile.
- **SAT/ACT plus AP** — competitive scores plus relevant AP sciences.

Mainland and international students should note that **clinical placements take place in Cantonese-speaking Hong Kong hospitals**. Conversational Cantonese ability is in practice essential for the clinical years, even though it is not formally tested at admission.

## Decision Framework: Should You Pick JS3612?

Pick JS3612 if you:

- Want a clinical career with direct patient contact but find medicine/dentistry too long, too costly, or too uncertain on JUPAS scoring.
- Are interested in imaging technology, AI in healthcare, or radiation oncology specifically.
- Value a degree with statutory registration baked in and near-100% graduate employment.
- Are willing to do shift work and clinical placements throughout your degree.

Look elsewhere if you:

- Want a research-heavy biomedical-sciences pathway (consider HKU/CUHK BSc in Biomedical Sciences instead).
- Cannot communicate in Cantonese and have no plans to learn — clinical training will be very difficult.
- Are squeamish about working with very ill, elderly, or dying patients (especially relevant for radiation therapy).

## Final Word

JS3612 is one of Hong Kong's most pragmatic degree choices: a single, focused, four-year route that ends with a registration certificate, a job offer, and a portable qualification. The JUPAS score required is real but achievable for a strong DSE candidate, and the long-term career trajectory — clinically, technically, and financially — is more secure than most undergraduate options at the same admission band. If healthcare without the seven-year medical track appeals to you, this should be high on your Band A list.

# Hong Kong Social Work Bachelor Complete Guide 2026: HKU JS6731, CUHK JS4874, PolyU JS3250, HKBU JS2660, CityU JS1113, SWRB Registration, ASWO Starting Salary HKD 36,850

Five UGC-funded universities in Hong Kong offer an undergraduate Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) degree that is recognised by the Social Workers Registration Board (SWRB) for direct registration as a Registered Social Worker (RSW): **The University of Hong Kong (HKU) JS6731**, **The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) JS4874**, **The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) JS3250**, **Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU) JS2660**, and **City University of Hong Kong (CityU) JS1113**. All five run for four years full-time, all five embed the SWRB-prescribed 800 hours of fieldwork practicum, and all five graduates can apply for RSW registration on the strength of the degree alone — without any further examination.

Social work is one of the few professions in Hong Kong where the labour market is structurally short of practitioners. The Social Welfare Department (SWD), the Hospital Authority's medical social services, the 165+ subvented NGOs that contract with SWD, the Lump Sum Grant (LSG) sector, and an expanding private and school-counselling market all compete for the same pool of new graduates. The 2023 Mental Health Review Report and the rollout of the District Services and Community Care Teams have added further demand. This guide breaks down all five JUPAS programmes in detail — admissions, curriculum, the RSW registration pathway, civil service and NGO pay, and overseas mobility — for 2026 DSE candidates choosing Band A.

## 1. Why social work is a structurally protected profession in Hong Kong

### 1.1 The Social Workers Registration Ordinance (Cap. 505)

Under **Cap. 505 of the Laws of Hong Kong (Social Workers Registration Ordinance)**, in force since 6 June 1997, only persons whose names appear on the SWRB register may use the title "Social Worker" or "社會工作者" or hold a position designated as a social worker post. The Board, established 16 January 1998, maintains the register, sets the Code of Practice, accredits qualifying programmes, and handles disciplinary inquiries.

To be registered, an applicant must:

1. Hold a SWRB-recognised social work qualification (one of the local BSW programmes listed in section 2, or an SWRB-assessed overseas qualification);
2. Be ordinarily resident in Hong Kong (the Board does not consider an RSW ordinarily resident if absent from Hong Kong for two years or more);
3. Satisfy fit-and-proper checks and pay the registration fee.

Unlike pharmacists, dentists, and physiotherapists, social workers do **not** sit a separate licensing examination — the SWRB-recognised degree itself is the qualifying credential. This makes the local BSW the single cleanest entry route to the profession.

### 1.2 Statutory job market protection

Because Cap. 505 reserves the title and the post designation, every job advertisement that names "Social Worker", "Assistant Social Work Officer", "Social Work Officer" or "Social Work Assistant" by SWD or any subvented NGO must be filled by an RSW. This produces the stable graduate employment rate (95%+ across all five universities) that distinguishes social work from many cognate humanities and social-science majors.

### 1.3 Two parallel pay tracks — civil service and NGO

A BSW graduate can be employed either:

- **Government civil service** as an Assistant Social Work Officer (ASWO) on the **Master Pay Scale (MPS) Point 16, currently HKD 36,850/month** (2024-2025 figure, reviewed annually by the Civil Service Bureau). Promotion to Social Work Officer (SWO), MPS 33-44, follows after several years of frontline experience and is a competitive internal promotion.
- **Subvented NGO** as a Social Worker on a "Social Worker pay scale" pegged to the SWD Lump Sum Grant model. Most large NGOs (Caritas, Tung Wah, HKSKH, Po Leung Kuk, Christian Family Service Centre, Yang Memorial, Methodist Centre etc.) place a fresh BSW on a starting point around MPS 14-16, broadly comparable to ASWO but with NGO-specific allowances, contract length, and welfare benefits.

Graduates also work in school social work, integrated family service centres (IFSCs), integrated children & youth service centres (ICYSCs), elderly homes, hospital medical social services, probation, drug rehabilitation, mental health residences, and a growing private counselling sector.

## 2. The five BSW programmes at a glance

| University | JUPAS Code | Programme name | Duration | Approx. annual intake | Median DSE (2024) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HKU | **JS6731** | Bachelor of Social Work | 4 years | ~50 | 27-29 (best 6) |
| CUHK | **JS4874** | Bachelor of Social Work (Honours) | 4 years | ~80 | 26-28 (best 5) |
| PolyU | **JS3250** | Bachelor of Arts (Honours) in Social Work | 4 years | ~110 | 23-25 (best 5) |
| HKBU | **JS2660** | Bachelor of Social Work (Honours) | 4 years | ~50 | 22-24 (best 6) |
| CityU | **JS1113** | Bachelor of Social Sciences (Honours) in Social Work | 4 years | ~60 | 23-25 (best 5) |

All five programmes appear on the SWRB's Lists of Recognized Qualifications under the heading "Hong Kong" and confer direct RSW eligibility. CityU and HKBU also operate a senior-year-entry (Year 3) BSW route for sub-degree holders, but the JUPAS DSE intake is to Year 1.

### 2.1 HKU JS6731 — Bachelor of Social Work

Offered by the Department of Social Work and Social Administration in the Faculty of Social Sciences. Curriculum integrates social policy, sociology, psychology, and social administration with social work methods (casework, group work, community work). Students complete two blocks of fieldwork (a 50-day Concurrent Field Practicum in Year 3 and a 80-day Block Field Practicum in Year 4), totalling the SWRB minimum of 800 supervised hours. HKU also offers a stream allowing dual focus on social work and Chinese medicine social services or mental health. Graduates frequently progress to Master of Social Sciences in Mental Health, MSW, or PhD.

### 2.2 CUHK JS4874 — Bachelor of Social Work (Honours)

Run by the Department of Social Work, Faculty of Social Science. Strong tradition in family therapy, community organisation, and Chinese cultural perspectives in social work. Year-1 admission combined with the College system (New Asia, Chung Chi, United, Shaw, Morningside, S.H. Ho, C.W. Chu, Wu Yee Sun, Lee Woo Sing). The Department was the first in Hong Kong to launch postgraduate clinical training and offers a strong articulation to its MSocSc in Family Counselling and the Master of Social Work. JUPAS interviews after DSE results in late July are mandatory for shortlisted Band A candidates.

### 2.3 PolyU JS3250 — Bachelor of Arts (Honours) in Social Work

Run by the Department of Applied Social Sciences. Largest single intake of the five, with the most diverse fieldwork placement network across rehabilitation, gerontology, school social work, youth at risk, and family service. PolyU's WIE (Work-Integrated Education) framework integrates the SWRB practicum hours with additional 80-hour service learning. Strong industrial reputation in the NGO sector — PolyU graduates are heavily represented in subvented agency middle management.

### 2.4 HKBU JS2660 — Bachelor of Social Work (Honours)

Run by the Department of Social Work, Faculty of Social Sciences. HKBU emphasises a Christian liberal-arts tradition (though admission is non-denominational) and has a notable specialism in family-life education, marriage and family enrichment, and community engagement. The four-year curriculum includes the SWRB-prescribed 800 hours of supervised fieldwork in Years 3 and 4. HKBU's Whole Person Education general-education core gives the BSW a strong humanities foundation.

### 2.5 CityU JS1113 — Bachelor of Social Sciences (Honours) in Social Work

Run by the Department of Social and Behavioural Sciences. Curriculum balances social work methods with quantitative social-research training (statistics, research methods) — useful for graduates aiming at programme evaluation, policy analysis, or graduate research. CityU also offers minors in Counselling, Public Policy, and Asian and International Studies that pair well with the BSW major. The 800-hour practicum is split between a Year-3 concurrent placement and a Year-4 block placement.

## 3. JUPAS admission — DSE scoring and interviews

### 3.1 Minimum admission requirements

All five programmes require the standard "**3-3-2-2-2**" or "**4C32**" entry profile under the New Senior Secondary academic structure: Chinese Language Level 3, English Language Level 3, Mathematics Compulsory Part Level 2, Citizenship and Social Development "Attained", plus two electives at Level 2 or above. Additional programme-specific weightings vary:

- **HKU JS6731** weights the best 6 subjects, with English typically given a x1.5 multiplier.
- **CUHK JS4874** uses best 5, English x1.5.
- **PolyU JS3250** uses best 5, English Level 3 minimum.
- **HKBU JS2660** uses best 6 with weighted English.
- **CityU JS1113** uses best 5, with bonuses for relevant electives.

Indicative median DSE scores in recent years sit in the range 23-29 depending on the school, with HKU and CUHK at the upper end. Liberal Studies/Citizenship and Social Development is now scored on Attained/Not Attained only.

### 3.2 The JUPAS interview

All five programmes interview shortlisted Band A applicants in late July, after DSE results are released. The format varies — HKU and CUHK use group discussion plus individual interview; PolyU and CityU use group interview; HKBU uses a combination. Common themes include:

- Why social work and not psychology/counselling/sociology?
- A current Hong Kong social issue (e.g., subdivided flats, sandwich-class poverty, elderly suicide, youth mental health, ethnic minority integration) — what is the social-work response?
- A short ethical scenario (e.g., a colleague breaches confidentiality; a service user expresses suicidal ideation; a mandatory reporting trigger).
- The applicant's volunteering or community service history.

Interviews are scored on motivation, communication, ethical reasoning, and Cantonese/English proficiency. There is no formal pre-reading list, but candidates should be familiar with the SWD Five-Year Plan, the major NGO families, and the most recent Policy Address sections on welfare.

## 4. The four-year curriculum and the 800-hour fieldwork requirement

All SWRB-recognised BSW programmes share a common skeleton dictated by the Board's **Principles, Criteria and Standards** (8th Edition, March 2022). The minimum requirements include:

1. **Generic foundation** — psychology (lifespan development, abnormal), sociology, social policy, research methods, Hong Kong social welfare history.
2. **Social work methods** — casework, group work, community work, integrated method, and at least one specialised method (family therapy, narrative, CBT, solution-focused).
3. **Fields of practice** — children & youth, family, gerontology, mental health, rehabilitation, medical, school, probation/correctional, addiction, ethnic minorities.
4. **Law and ethics** — Cap. 505 ordinance, SWRB Code of Practice, Mental Health Ordinance Cap. 136, Mental Capacity Bill, Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance, child protection legislation.
5. **Fieldwork practicum** — minimum **800 supervised hours** in two or more SWRB-registered placement agencies, supervised by a Field Instructor who is an RSW with at least three years of post-qualification experience. Most universities split this into a concurrent (part-time, alongside lectures) and a block (full-time) placement.

Failing the practicum prevents graduation regardless of academic GPA, and a serious ethical breach during practicum can be referred to the SWRB.

## 5. Becoming a Registered Social Worker (RSW)

The post-graduation registration process is straightforward but must be completed before any "Social Worker" job offer can be confirmed:

1. **Submit Form A** to the SWRB with the BSW transcript, degree certificate, three passport photos, HKID copy, and the registration fee.
2. The Board verifies the qualification against its recognised list (all five JUPAS programmes are pre-listed, so verification is administrative rather than substantive).
3. The Board issues an RSW certificate and adds the applicant to the public register (searchable at swrb.org.hk).
4. The RSW must thereafter renew **annually** and notify the Board of any change of address within one month.
5. Failure to reside in Hong Kong for two consecutive years ends "ordinarily resident" status and triggers removal from the register; re-registration on return is possible but requires fresh application.

Disciplinary jurisdiction includes professional misconduct, criminal convictions, and breaches of the Code. Sanctions range from reprimand to deregistration.

## 6. Civil service and NGO salary in 2026

### 6.1 Assistant Social Work Officer (ASWO) — civil service

ASWO is the entry-level civil service post for BSW graduates. As of the latest Civil Service Bureau Master Pay Scale (effective 1 April 2024 and rolled forward in 2025-2026 unless revised):

| Rank | MPS Points | Approximate monthly salary |
|---|---|---|
| ASWO (entry) | MPS 16 | **HKD 36,850** |
| ASWO (mid) | MPS 17-22 | HKD 38,755 – HKD 53,055 |
| Social Work Officer | MPS 33-44 | HKD 79,140 – HKD 124,180 |
| Senior Social Work Officer | MPS 45-49 | HKD 130,500 – HKD 156,420 |

Civil service ASWO posts are advertised by the Civil Service Bureau several rounds a year and are extremely competitive — typical entry ratios of 30:1 to 50:1 applicants per post. Successful candidates take a Common Recruitment Examination (English, Chinese, Aptitude) and a structured interview.

### 6.2 NGO Social Worker

The 165+ subvented NGOs employ the majority of BSW graduates. Pay is broadly pegged to MPS but specific to each NGO's HR scheme. Indicative starting monthly salaries in 2026 range from **HKD 33,000 to HKD 38,500**, generally rising to HKD 45,000-55,000 after five years of frontline experience and to HKD 65,000+ for unit-in-charge or senior worker roles. Shift allowances apply for residential care and emergency 24-hour services.

### 6.3 Specialist routes

Hospital Authority Medical Social Workers, court-attached probation officers (Social Welfare Department), school social workers under the SWD/Education Bureau scheme, and Correctional Services Department welfare officers all map to government MPS scales similar to ASWO. Private practice (counselling, EAP, family mediation) and corporate social responsibility roles tend to be paid by hourly or contract rates.

## 7. Overseas recognition and mobility

A SWRB-recognised Hong Kong BSW does **not** automatically qualify in other jurisdictions, but most major systems accept it through assessment:

- **United Kingdom — Social Work England**: Hong Kong BSW graduates apply via the International Application for Registration. Most are required to complete an Overseas Social Work Qualification assessment, an English language test (IELTS 7.0 generally), and may be asked to complete a Test of Competence or supervised return-to-practice.
- **Australia — AASW**: graduates apply for Overseas Qualifications Assessment with the Australian Association of Social Workers. Hong Kong BSWs have been routinely recognised at "Eligible for AASW membership" subject to documentation; some applicants with shorter practicums are required to complete additional supervised hours.
- **Canada — CASW / provincial colleges**: each province has its own College of Social Workers (OCSWSSW in Ontario, BCCSW in BC, etc.). Hong Kong BSWs typically need a Canadian Council on Social Work Regulators credential assessment and may need to sit the Association of Social Work Boards (ASWB) examination at Bachelor or Master level.
- **Mainland China**: the Ministry of Civil Affairs Social Worker Vocational Qualification Examination (社工師) is a separate national exam unrelated to Cap. 505; Hong Kong RSWs interested in the Greater Bay Area must sit the Mainland exam and meet residence requirements.
- **Singapore — SASW / Allied Health Professions Council**: post-2021, Singapore moved to statutory registration for social workers; Hong Kong BSWs apply through SASW credentialing.

For graduates considering postgraduate study, the **Master of Social Work (MSW)** at HKU, CUHK, PolyU, HKBU, or CityU is the natural progression for those without a BSW (a one-to-two-year qualifying degree); for those who already hold the BSW, a coursework or research master in **family therapy, mental health, gerontology, or counselling** adds specialism. PhD pathways through the same departments lead to academic, policy-research, and senior NGO management roles.

## 8. How to choose between the five programmes

**Choose HKU JS6731** if you want the smallest cohort, the strongest research culture, and a broad social-administration foundation.

**Choose CUHK JS4874** if you want the family-therapy specialism, the College system, and a strong articulation to MSW or counselling masters.

**Choose PolyU JS3250** if you want the largest placement network, the most diverse fieldwork, and a clear NGO career trajectory.

**Choose HKBU JS2660** if you want a humanities-rich liberal-arts foundation, family-life education focus, and a smaller-group teaching style.

**Choose CityU JS1113** if you want strong quantitative research training alongside social work practice, useful for policy and evaluation careers.

All five lead to the same RSW credential and broadly the same starting salary. The differences lie in cohort culture, research focus, placement networks, and elective options. 2026 DSE candidates should rank all five in JUPAS Band A or B according to predicted score and personal fit, and prepare thoroughly for the interview round in late July.

# Hong Kong Speech-Language Pathology Bachelor (HKU JS6157) Complete Guide 2026 - The Only Local Direct-Registration Pathway, Five-Year Curriculum, 300+ Clinical Hours, HKIST Registration, Hospital Authority Salary Scales and Career Prospects

If you are scanning Hong Kong's allied-health degrees for the "unicorn" programme - a single-cohort, ultra-selective course where every graduate walks straight into a regulated profession - the Bachelor of Science in Speech-Language Pathology (Honours) at the University of Hong Kong (HKU), formerly known as the Bachelor of Science in Speech and Hearing Sciences, JUPAS code **JS6157**, has to be on the shortlist. It is the **only** undergraduate speech-therapy degree in Hong Kong, the only local route to register as a Speech Therapist on the Department of Health's Accredited Register, and it admits roughly 48 students per year - making it as selective as Medicine and Dentistry on most JUPAS dashboards.

This guide, written for the 2026 JUPAS admission cycle, covers the curriculum structure, entry requirements, Cantonese-English language demands, interview format, clinical placement (300+ supervised hours), HKIST registration pathway, Hospital Authority Speech Therapist salaries, graduate destinations, and overseas mobility for HKU graduates - in one read.

## 1. Why Speech-Language Pathology Is a "Unicorn" Major in Hong Kong

Speech-language pathologists (SLPs, locally called Speech Therapists) work across the full age spectrum:

- **Paediatric** caseload: late-talkers, developmental language disorder, autism-spectrum communication, articulation/phonology, stuttering, literacy difficulties, cleft palate speech.
- **Adult acquired** caseload: post-stroke aphasia and dysarthria, traumatic brain injury, head-and-neck cancer (post-laryngectomy voice and swallowing), Parkinson's, motor neurone disease, dementia communication support.
- **Voice and upper airway**: professional voice users, vocal fold pathology, transgender voice, tracheostomy and ventilator weaning support.
- **Dysphagia (swallowing)**: instrumental assessment (VFSS, FEES) and rehabilitation across acute, sub-acute and community settings.
- **Hearing-impaired** children, working alongside audiologists to develop spoken language.

With Hong Kong's rapidly ageing population, expanding stroke and dementia caseloads, and a growing special-school sector, demand for SLPs in the Hospital Authority (HA), Department of Health, special schools, NGO rehabilitation centres and private practice consistently outstrips supply. Yet **HKU is the only institution in Hong Kong offering an undergraduate speech-therapy degree** - PolyU, CUHK, EdUHK and CityU do not. Anyone wanting to register locally without studying abroad must come through JS6157. This single-pipeline reality is why the cut-off score sits with Medicine and Dentistry rather than with most allied-health programmes.

## 2. Programme Snapshot

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Full title | Bachelor of Science in Speech-Language Pathology (Honours) |
| Host faculty | Faculty of Education, HKU |
| JUPAS code | JS6157 |
| Duration | 5 years full-time |
| Year-1 intake | ~48 students (not pre-determined; depends on applicant quality) |
| Funding | UGC-funded |
| Year-1 tuition (local) | ~HK$47,000 |
| Language of instruction | Academic curriculum in English; clinical training conducted **primarily in Cantonese** |
| Professional accreditation | Hong Kong Institute of Speech Therapists (HKIST) |
| Registration route | Graduates eligible to apply for Speech Therapist in the DH Accredited Register |

The 2017 rename from "Speech and Hearing Sciences" to "Speech-Language Pathology" aligns the programme's nomenclature with North American conventions, while content scope still covers the full SLP remit including voice, fluency and dysphagia. This naming and content alignment also smooths credential recognition with Speech Pathology Australia (SPA), the New Zealand Speech-language Therapists' Association (NZSTA) and several Canadian provinces.

## 3. Five-Year Curriculum at a Glance

The programme follows a translational-learning model: foundational sciences first, integrated clinical reasoning in the middle years, and a heavy clinical-plus-research load in the final two years.

### Year 1 - Foundations
- Anatomy and physiology of speech, hearing and swallowing
- Phonetics and Cantonese/English linguistics
- Introduction to communication disorders
- Common Core Curriculum (HKU university-wide requirement)
- Early observation placements in clinics and schools

### Year 2 - Building Clinical Science
- Language acquisition and development (Cantonese and English)
- Audiology fundamentals and screening
- Neuroanatomy and neurology for SLPs
- Statistics and research methods
- Small-group case-based learning begins

### Year 3 - Disorder-Focused Modules
- Paediatric speech and language disorders
- Adult acquired language disorders (aphasia)
- Motor speech disorders (dysarthria, apraxia)
- Fluency disorders (stuttering, cluttering)
- Voice disorders
- Initial supervised clinical placements with real clients

### Year 4 - Specialisation and Internship
- Dysphagia assessment and management
- Cleft palate and craniofacial disorders
- Augmentative and alternative communication (AAC)
- Counselling and inter-professional practice
- External clinical block placements (hospitals, special schools, NGOs)

### Year 5 - Capstone
- Final-year research project (empirical thesis)
- Advanced clinical placements
- Professional issues, ethics, and the HKIST Code of Practice
- Preparation for the HKIST registration application

Total supervised clinical hours exceed **300** across the five years, surpassing the minima required by HKIST and most overseas regulators.

## 4. JUPAS Admission Requirements 2026

### Minimum HKDSE requirements

| Subject | Required Level |
| --- | --- |
| English Language | 5 |
| Chinese Language | 4 |
| Mathematics (Compulsory Part) | 3 |
| Citizenship and Social Development | Attained |
| Elective 1 | 4 |
| Elective 2 | 3 |

Biology is **strongly recommended** but not compulsory. Successful applicants commonly bring Biology plus one of Chemistry, Physics, Psychology (M2 also helps for the research-methods component), and most carry a 5* or 5** in English given the bilingual demand.

### Score calculation (Best-5 weighting)

HKU JS6157 uses a Best-5 calculation with English **x1.5** and Mathematics (Compulsory) **x0.5**. Recent admission cohorts have settled around **27-30 (Best-5)** at the median, with the lower 10th percentile near 26 and the upper 10th near 32 - placing JS6157 in the same league as MBBS at HKU/CUHK and BDS at HKU.

## 5. Selection: Band A, Interview, and Cantonese Fluency

Only applicants who place **JS6157 in Band A** and meet the academic minima are shortlisted for interview. Two filters then apply:

1. **Academic merit** - DSE score, with weight on English and any science electives.
2. **Interview performance**, weighted heavily.

The interview is conducted partly in **Cantonese** and partly in English. Expect a structured panel covering:

- Why speech therapy, why HKU, and what you understand about the profession's scope (red flags: confusing SLP with English-language teaching or with audiology).
- Ethical scenarios (e.g., disagreeing with a parent about a child's intervention plan).
- Brief language tasks to gauge bilingual fluency, articulation and listening discrimination - applicants must be able to take a clinical history in conversational Cantonese.
- Personality and team-fit cues; SLPs work daily with parents, teachers, doctors, OTs, PTs, audiologists.

**Cantonese fluency is not optional.** Hong Kong's clinical caseload is overwhelmingly Cantonese-speaking, and supervisors will not place a student on a Cantonese ward if their Cantonese cannot support an assessment. Mandarin speakers from the Mainland or overseas-returnee applicants who are not yet conversational in Cantonese should plan a year of intensive Cantonese before applying, or consider non-JUPAS routes only after demonstrable proficiency.

## 6. Clinical Placement: 300+ Hours Across Five Years

Placements are arranged by HKU's clinical education team and rotate students through:

- **Hospital Authority** acute and rehabilitation wards (paediatric and adult)
- **Department of Health** Child Assessment Centres and special preschool services
- **Special schools** (physical disability, intellectual disability, hearing impairment)
- **NGO** rehabilitation and elderly day-care centres
- **HKU Speech Therapy Clinic** (on-campus teaching clinic)
- Selected **private practices** for breadth in paediatric and voice work

Each placement is supervised by a registered Speech Therapist and counts toward the HKIST registration minima. Students receive structured competency assessments using the Hong Kong adaptation of the COMPASS framework (or its successor used by HKU at the time of placement).

## 7. HKIST Registration After Graduation

The Hong Kong Institute of Speech Therapists (HKIST) operates the Department of Health's Accredited Register for speech therapists. HKU JS6157 is the only Hong Kong undergraduate programme **directly accredited** by HKIST - graduates apply for the Accredited Register without sitting a separate qualifying examination, provided clinical hours and academic standing are met.

Maintaining registration requires annual continuing professional development (CPD) hours and renewal under the HKIST Code of Practice. Hospital Authority and Department of Health employment offers are typically conditional on Accredited-Register status.

## 8. Hospital Authority Speech Therapist Salary 2026

The Hospital Authority salary scale for newly qualified speech therapists generally follows the **Master Pay Scale (MPS) Point 16 starting**, rising on the standard increment ladder. As of 2026:

- **Speech Therapist (entry, MPS Point 16)** - approximately HK$44,000 - HK$48,000 per month, plus contractual end-of-contract gratuity for fixed-term appointments and pension/MPF contributions for permanent appointments.
- **Senior Speech Therapist** - typically reached after 6-10 years of service plus internal selection; mid-MPS range with additional managerial allowance.

Private-practice rates vary widely. Recently graduated SLPs in established paediatric clinics earn HK$40,000-50,000 per month rising quickly with caseload, while senior independent practitioners with established referral networks can earn substantially more. NGO and special-school rates broadly track the HA scale, sometimes with allowances for rural or specialised settings.

Public reference points cited by salary aggregators put the Hong Kong Speech Therapist average around **HK$43,000-45,000 per month** in 2026, consistent with the HA-weighted distribution of the workforce.

## 9. Graduate Destinations

Typical first-job destinations for JS6157 graduates:

- **Hospital Authority** (the largest single employer): acute hospitals, rehab hospitals, community geriatric assessment teams.
- **Department of Health**: Child Assessment Centres, Maternal & Child Health, special preschool services.
- **Special schools** (subvented by the Education Bureau).
- **NGO rehabilitation centres** (Heep Hong Society, SAHK, Caritas, etc.).
- **Private clinics** focusing on paediatric language and literacy, adult voice, or international-school caseloads.
- **Academia / research** via PhD, particularly for students who excel in the Year-5 thesis.

A growing minority pursue cross-border practice in the Greater Bay Area, particularly in international schools and private rehabilitation networks in Shenzhen, Guangzhou and Macau, where HKU graduates command a premium for their English-Cantonese-Mandarin skill set.

## 10. Overseas Recognition and Mobility

Because HKU's curriculum aligns with the SLP scope used internationally, graduates have been able to register or qualify (with assessment) in:

- **Australia** - Speech Pathology Australia (SPA), via the Overseas-Qualified SLP assessment route. HKU graduates are well-represented among internationally-qualified members.
- **New Zealand** - NZSTA, via portfolio assessment and possibly bridging coursework.
- **United Kingdom** - Royal College of Speech and Language Therapists (RCSLT) and HCPC, typically via the international application route.
- **Canada** - SAC and provincial regulators (e.g., CASLPO in Ontario) generally require a master's-level qualification, so HKU graduates often progress via a North American MSc/MA before registering.
- **United States** - ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC-SLP) requires a master's degree in the US system; HKU's bachelor's serves as a strong foundation for that pathway.

A useful mental model: HKU's BSc(SLP) is treated as **entry-to-practice** in jurisdictions whose entry-level qualification is a bachelor's (Hong Kong, Australia, NZ, UK), and as a **strong undergraduate prerequisite** in master's-entry jurisdictions (US, Canada).

## 11. Non-JUPAS, Mainland and Overseas Routes

International and Mainland applicants apply through HKU's non-JUPAS channel using IB, A-Level, Gaokao, SAT/ACT, or equivalent qualifications. Indicative thresholds in recent cycles:

- **IB** - 41+ with HL 6,6,6 typical for shortlisting; English HL 6 and a science HL strongly preferred.
- **A-Level** - A*A*A typical, with English-language proficiency separately assessed.
- **Gaokao** - admission via HKU's Mainland scheme, but **Cantonese fluency by interview** remains the binding constraint - applicants without conversational Cantonese are unlikely to be admitted to JS6157 regardless of academic profile.
- **IELTS / TOEFL** - IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or TOEFL iBT 100+ typically required.

## 12. Cost of Study (Local UGC-Funded Track)

| Year | Tuition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Year 1-5 | ~HK$47,000 / year | UGC-funded local rate |
| Living | HK$60,000-100,000 / year | If hall-resident; higher off-campus |
| Books and clinical kit | ~HK$5,000 / year | Tuning forks, oral exam mirrors, recording app subscriptions |
| Placement transport | ~HK$3,000-6,000 / year | Cross-territory travel during clinical blocks |

Government Tertiary Student Finance Scheme (TSFS) loans and grants are available to eligible local students.

## 13. Application Timeline 2026

| Date | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Sep-Dec 2025 | JUPAS account opening, programme research, Cantonese-fluency self-audit |
| Early Dec 2025 | JUPAS application deadline (initial choices) |
| Apr 2026 | DSE examinations |
| May 2026 | JUPAS Programme Choice Modification (after DSE) - final Band A allocation |
| Jun-Jul 2026 | HKU JS6157 interview rounds for shortlisted applicants |
| Aug 2026 | JUPAS Main Round results released |
| Sep 2026 | Year-1 commences at HKU |

## 14. Should You Apply? Honest Self-Test

**Apply if you can answer "yes" to all of the following:**

1. Your DSE forecast is in the 27-32 Best-5 range (with English at 5* or above), or you have an equivalent IB/A-Level profile.
2. You are conversationally fluent in **Cantonese** - able to take a 30-minute case history without a script.
3. You can articulate a concrete reason for SLP rather than Medicine, Audiology, Psychology or English Education.
4. You are comfortable with five years of intense clinical training, including frequent evaluation and feedback on your own communication style.
5. You are willing to commit to a regulated profession with annual CPD and ethical oversight.

**Reconsider if** you are using JS6157 only as a "Medicine fallback" - the interview panel will spot this within minutes, and the workload is too heavy to sustain without genuine motivation.

## 15. Bottom Line

HKU's Bachelor of Science in Speech-Language Pathology (JS6157) is Hong Kong's **only** local undergraduate route into a fast-growing, regulated allied-health profession with strong Hospital Authority demand, robust private-practice options, and good overseas mobility. The combination of a Medicine-level cut-off, mandatory Cantonese fluency, 300+ supervised clinical hours, and a five-year duration filters tightly for vocation-driven students - but for those students, JS6157 offers career certainty that few other JUPAS programmes can match.

If you have the DSE profile, the Cantonese, and a clear answer to "why speech therapy?", JS6157 belongs at the top of your Band A. If any of the three is missing, build it deliberately over the next admission cycle - and consider an overseas master's-entry route as a parallel option.
